concepts/derivedUnits.label: derived units
concepts/derivedUnits.summary: the units of a quantity or of a formula as they follow from the model
concepts/derivedUnits.description:
A model does not have to declare units everywhere: a compartment, a species or a parameter inherits the units of the model when it declares none, and the units of a formula follow from the units of the elements it uses. The report derives the units which follow from the model, reduces them to base units with their exponent, scale and multiplier, and renders the result as a formula. A quantity without a dimension reads `dimensionless`, and a dash says that the units are not declared or that the model does not say enough to derive them.

Derived units are shown in the column "derived units" of the tables and in the inspector. They are the fastest check whether a kinetic law is dimensionally what it should be, because the derived units of a kinetic law are extent per time when the law is right.

concepts/equation.label: equation
concepts/equation.summary: the reaction written as a chemical equation
concepts/equation.description:
The report writes every reaction as its reactants, an arrow and its products, with the stoichiometry in front of a species when it is not one, a minus in front of it when the stoichiometry is minus one, and the identifier of the species reference, or a question mark, when the stoichiometry is set by a rule instead of by a number. The arrow is a double arrow when the reaction is reversible and a single arrow when it is not.

The equation is a column of the table of reactions and a row of the inspector of a reaction, and it is what makes a list of reactions readable without opening any of them.

concepts/manifest.label: manifest
concepts/manifest.summary: the entries of the COMBINE archive a report was built from
concepts/manifest.description:
A COMBINE archive holds the files of a modelling study with a manifest which names every entry, its format and whether it is a master file. The report is built for every SBML entry of the archive, and a plain SBML file which is submitted on its own is wrapped in an archive with one master entry, so that a report always comes with a manifest.

The manifest decides which report is shown first: the master entry when that entry has a report, and the first entry otherwise, because an archive does not have to mark one. It is also what the report offers when an archive holds more than one model.

concepts/math.label: rendered math
concepts/math.summary: the formula of an element as the report renders it
concepts/math.description:
SBML stores a formula as content MathML, which is precise and unreadable. The report turns it into the typeset formula a textbook would print, with fractions, powers, subscripts for the parts of a name and greek letters where a name is one, and keeps the same expression as an infix formula next to it, so that it can be read and copied as text.

The rendered formula is the column "math" of the tables of rules, function definitions, constraints and events, the kinetic law of a reaction, and the mathematics shown in the inspector. Where a formula names an element of the model, the report also links that element as a link of the kind "math".

concepts/modelKind.label: model kind
concepts/modelKind.summary: whether a model is the model of the document or a model definition
concepts/modelKind.description:
A document contains at most one model, but the comp package adds model definitions, which exist to be instantiated by a submodel and are not simulated themselves. The report reads both and marks every model as `model` or `modelDefinition`.

The kind is shown in the attributes of a model. The report opens the model of the document first and lets the model definitions be selected next to it.

concepts/number.label: number
concepts/number.summary: how the report shows a number which is infinite or not a number
concepts/number.description:
A double of SBML may be infinite or not a number, `INF`, `-INF` and `NaN` as a file writes them, and both are ordinary values: the upper bound of an unbounded flux is `INF`, and a `NaN` says that a quantity is defined but its number is not known. JSON has no literal for either of them, so the report sends them as the three constants `"Infinity"`, `"-Infinity"` and `"NaN"`, which keeps them apart from `null`, the attribute a file does not set at all.

The report shows an infinite value as the sign of infinity with the direction of its bound, ∞ and -∞, with the `INF` or `-INF` of the file as its tooltip, and a value which is not a number as `NaN`. An attribute which is not set stays the dash every empty cell of the report shows. Every other number is shown with six significant digits, and the full number is the tooltip of the rounded one.

concepts/pk.label: primary key
concepts/pk.summary: the identifier the report gives to every element it shows
concepts/pk.description:
SBML identifies an element by its id, which is unique within one model, and many elements of a model have no id at all. The report therefore builds a key of its own for every element, of the form `<scope>/<type>:<id>`: the scope, which is the model the element belongs to or the document for an element of the document, the type of the element and its id. An element without an id falls back to the element it sets, for an [initial assignment](glossary:types/InitialAssignment) or a rule, then to its meta id, and then to a key of what it is about: an element nested in another one is keyed after its parent and what it names, a reactant after its reaction and its species (`Reaction1.reactant.X`), a replacement after its element, its submodel and the element it reaches, a measure of an uncertainty after its type (`u_Km.standardDeviation`), a [list](glossary:types/ListOf) after its owner and its name in the file (`J0.listOfReactants`, and `listOfRules` for a list of the model), and an element which names nothing, an algebraic rule, a constraint, an event or a transition, after its place among the elements of its type (`algebraicRule.0`). Where a list repeats such a key, a species which a reaction lists twice among its reactants, the repetition is told apart by its occurrence (`Reaction1.reactant.X.1`). The model of a document without an id is scoped as `model`, and only an element which the specification requires an id of, and which the file leaves without one, is keyed by a digest of its XML.

The primary key is what the links of a report point at and what the url of a report names when an element is selected. An element without an id is shown by the key alone, without the scope and the type in front of it, in the header of the inspector and as the label of every link to it. An element which the file nests in another one is named after that element and its place in it instead, because a meta id says nothing about where it sits: the kinetic law of `Reaction1` reads `Reaction1.kineticLaw`, the trigger of the event `Start` reads `Start.trigger`, an assignment of that event to `kp` reads `Start.kp`, a reactant `X` of `Reaction1` reads `Reaction1.X` and the list of the reactants of `Reaction1` reads `Reaction1.listOfReactants`.

concepts/sbmlType.label: sbml type
concepts/sbmlType.summary: the kind of element, which decides how the report shows it
concepts/sbmlType.description:
Every element of a report carries the name of its SBML class, for example `Species`, `AssignmentRule` or `Objective`. The report groups the elements of a model by it, and it decides the section of the report, the colour and the icon of the type mark, the columns of the table and the attributes the inspector shows.

The type is shown as the mark in front of every element, as the header of every section of the report and in the header of the inspector.

concepts/targetEntry.label: link into another document
concepts/targetEntry.summary: a link which ends at an element of another entry of the archive
concepts/targetEntry.description:
The links of a report stay inside one SBML document, with one exception: a model of the comp package may instantiate a model of another document through an [external model definition](glossary:types/ExternalModelDefinition), and its [replacements](glossary:types/ReplacedElement), [deletions](glossary:types/Deletion) and [ports](glossary:types/Port) then name elements of that document. Where the other document is part of the report, as another entry of the same COMBINE archive, the link ends at the element inside it.

Such a link shows the file name of the other entry next to the element, and following it opens the report of that entry. The element lists the link under "Referenced by" with the file name of the entry it comes from.

concepts/unitsLatex.label: rendered units
concepts/unitsLatex.summary: the units an element declares, rendered as a formula
concepts/unitsLatex.description:
A units attribute names a unit definition, and a unit definition is a list of base units with an exponent, a scale and a multiplier. The report resolves the reference and renders the product as a formula, so that a table shows millimole over litre as a fraction instead of the identifier `mmol_per_l`, next to the identifier it comes from.

The rendered units appear in the units columns of the tables, in the units of the inspector and in the units column of the table of unit definitions, whose inspector shows them as the formula above the units the definition is built from.

datatypes/Association.label: Association
datatypes/Association.summary: one node of the gene association of a reaction, of the three kinds the package defines
datatypes/Association.description:
`Association` is the abstract class of the nodes a [gene product association](glossary:types/GeneProductAssociation) is built from. It is never written as an element of its own: every node is one of its three subclasses, an [and](glossary:types/And), an [or](glossary:types/Or) or a [gene product reference](glossary:types/GeneProductRef), and the name of the element is the name of that class with a small first letter. An `and` and an `or` hold two or more associations of their own, which is what makes the class recursive and the association of a reaction a tree of any depth.

The report gives every node an element of its own and renders the tree as the expression it stands for, with a link at every gene product it names. The association which the example of Section 3.9 encodes, an `or` of three complexes, reads `((g_b3670 and g_b3671) or (g_b0077 and g_b0078) or (g_b3768 and g_b3769 and g_b3767))` in the report: the expression is written with the identifiers the references hold, not with the labels the reconstruction knows the genes by.

datatypes/CompSBase.label: CompSBase
datatypes/CompSBase.summary: what the comp package adds to an element, the replacements it takes part in
datatypes/CompSBase.description:
The report keeps the two subcomponents the comp package adds to every element in one block: the [replaced elements](glossary:types/ReplacedElement), the elements of submodels which this element takes the place of, and the [replaced by](glossary:types/ReplacedBy), the element of a submodel which takes the place of this one. An element may carry both, and an element which takes part in no replacement carries neither.

The inspector shows the block as two rows of the element: [comp:replacedBy](glossary:types/SBase/comp.replacedBy), the submodel and the element inside it which takes the place of this one, and [comp:listOfReplacedElements](glossary:types/SBase/comp.replacedElements), a table with one row per replacement, each naming its submodel and the element it replaces. Every one of these names is a link to the element it stands for.

datatypes/FbcOperation.label: FbcOperation
datatypes/FbcOperation.summary: how a flux bound of Version 1 relates the flux of a reaction to its value
datatypes/FbcOperation.description:
Version 1 of the package wrote a constraint of a flux as a [flux bound](glossary:types/FluxBound) of the model, one (in)equality of the form reaction, operator, value, and the operator is an attribute of this type: `R5 >= 0`, `R5 <= INF` and `R7 = 1.0` are three such bounds. Version 2 removed the construct and the type with it, because a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) names the [parameters](glossary:types/Parameter) of its lower and its upper bound instead, and which of the two a bound is follows from the attribute which names it.

The report shows the operation in the column "operation" of the flux bounds of a Version 1 model and next to the value in the inspector. The three values are the mathematical symbols `<=`, `>=` and `=`, in this order:

datatypes/FbcType.label: FbcType
datatypes/FbcType.summary: the sense of an objective, the direction in which it is optimised
datatypes/FbcType.description:
The [type](glossary:types/Objective/type) of an [objective](glossary:types/Objective) is the sense of the optimality constraint: whether an analysis looks for the flux distribution which makes the weighted sum of the fluxes as large as the bounds allow, or as small. Nothing else of the package carries the type, and the package has defined it with the same two values since Version 1.

The report shows the value as the file writes it, in the column "type" of the objectives of a model and in the inspector of an objective. The two values are:

datatypes/FbcVariableType.label: FbcVariableType
datatypes/FbcVariableType.summary: whether a term of a sum is linear or quadratic in its variable
datatypes/FbcVariableType.description:
Version 3 of the package added the type so that a [flux objective](glossary:types/FluxObjective) and a [component](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent) of a user defined constraint say how their variable enters the sum. A linear term is the variable multiplied by its coefficient, `C * J`; a quadratic term is the square of the variable, `C * J^2`, or the product of the two variables where the term names a second one, `C * J1 * J2`. Without the attribute the two cannot be told apart, which is why Version 3 requires it; a document of Version 1 or Version 2 has no such attribute and every term of it is linear.

The report writes a term as the product it is, with a superscript two on a quadratic variable which stands alone and with the second variable next to the first where the term names one. The two values are:

datatypes/ID.label: ID
datatypes/ID.summary: an identifier which is unique in the whole file
datatypes/ID.description:
`ID` is the identifier type of XML 1.0, which SBML takes over unchanged: `ID ::= ( letter | '_' | ':' ) NameChar*`, where a `NameChar` is a letter, a digit, `.`, `-`, `_`, `:`, a combining character or an extender, and where a letter is one of the upper and lower case letters of the Latin alphabet together with the many related characters Unicode 2.0 defines. Every value of this type lives in one namespace which spans the whole document, whatever element carries it and however deeply that element is nested, so no two elements of a file may carry the same one.

The [metaid](glossary:types/SBase/metaId) of an element is the only attribute of the core with this type, and the RDF of an [annotation](glossary:types/SBase/cvterms) names the element it describes by it. A meta id which is used twice makes the file invalid, and an annotation which names a meta id no element carries describes nothing. The report shows the meta id in the attributes of the inspector and falls back to it to name an element which has no id.

datatypes/IDREF.label: IDREF
datatypes/IDREF.summary: a reference to an element of the document by its meta id
datatypes/IDREF.description:
`IDREF` is the companion the XML Schema 1.0 specification gives to the type [ID](glossary:datatypes/ID): its value has the syntax of an `ID` and has to be the `ID` of an element defined elsewhere in a referenced document. Which document that is follows from the reference: it is the document the referenced model resides in, this file for a model definition of it and another file for an external model definition, and the value has to name an element inside that model. A meta id is unique in the whole file and not, like an identifier, in one model, so a value of this type names one element of a document without saying which instantiation of it is meant, which is what the comp package states per reference: the same element may be instantiated in many submodels.

The [metaIdRef](glossary:types/SBaseRef/metaIdRef) of a port, a deletion or a replacement is the attribute of this type, and it is how an element which carries no identifier of its own is named, a rule or a reaction written without one. The report searches the element with that meta id in the model the reference reaches into and links it.

datatypes/Math.label: Math
datatypes/Math.summary: a formula of the model in the two renderings the report gives it
datatypes/Math.description:
SBML writes every formula as content MathML, which is exact and unreadable. The report converts each formula once and keeps two renderings of it: the latex which the page typesets the way a textbook prints a formula, and the same expression in the infix notation of Level 3, `k1 * S1 - k2 * S2`, which is one line of text and can be copied into another tool.

Every formula the report shows is of this kind: the kinetic law of a reaction, the formula of a function definition, of an initial assignment, of a rule, of a constraint and of an event assignment, the trigger, the delay and the priority of an event, the condition of a function term of the qual package and the math of a parameter of an uncertainty of the distrib package. A table and the inspector show the typeset formula, the infix formula is its tooltip and what a click copies, and a formula too long to typeset stays text, which the inspector offers to render on demand where it shows the formula on a line of its own, while a table leaves it as it is. [Rendered math](glossary:concepts/math) describes this, and every element a formula names becomes a link of the kind [math](glossary:links/math).

datatypes/ModelFbc.label: ModelFbc
datatypes/ModelFbc.summary: what the fbc package adds to a model, its strictness and its active objective
datatypes/ModelFbc.description:
The report keeps the two attributes which fbc gives a model as a whole in one block: whether the model keeps to the restrictions of a strict problem, and which of its [objectives](glossary:types/Objective) is the one an analysis optimises. The second of them is an attribute of the list of objectives and not of the model, and the report carries a list as an object of its own only where it states something an `SBase` states, which is why the two are shown together.

The inspector shows the block as two rows of the model, [fbc:strict](glossary:types/Model/fbc.strict) and [fbc:activeObjective](glossary:types/Model/fbc.activeObjective), the second a link to the objective it names. The lists which fbc adds to a model are sections of the report and not part of this block.

datatypes/ModelHistory.label: ModelHistory
datatypes/ModelHistory.summary: who created an element and when it was changed
datatypes/ModelHistory.description:
The standard annotation of an element may carry its history, written in RDF: the terms of Dublin Core name the creators of the element, the date it was created and one date for every time it was changed, and inside a creator the name, the organisation and the electronic mail address are written with the terms of vCard. The report reads that block out of the annotation and keeps it as one value of the element, instead of leaving it in the XML for a reader to decipher.

Most files carry a history on the model alone, where it is the closest thing a model has to an author line. The report shows the creators with their organisation and their address, the date of creation and every date of modification, below the annotations in the inspector of the element.

datatypes/PortSIdRef.label: PortSIdRef
datatypes/PortSIdRef.summary: a reference to a port of a model by its identifier
datatypes/PortSIdRef.description:
The identifier of a [port](glossary:types/Port) is of the type `PortSId`, which the comp package derives from [SId](glossary:datatypes/SId): the syntax is that of an identifier, and the values live in a space of their own which spans the ports of one model. A port may therefore carry the identifier a species of the same model carries, without the two colliding and without one naming the other. An attribute of type `PortSIdRef` holds such a value, and it has to be the identifier of a port of the model the reference reaches into, not of the model which writes the reference.

A [deletion](glossary:types/Deletion), a [replaced element](glossary:types/ReplacedElement), a [replaced by](glossary:types/ReplacedBy) and every link of a nested [reference](glossary:types/SBaseRef) name their element in exactly one of four ways, by port, by identifier, by unit identifier or by meta id, and a replaced element by a deletion as well; the port reference is the way which goes through the interface the other model offers instead of reaching past it. A [port](glossary:types/Port) itself has only the other three, because no port may name a port of its own model; it reaches a port of one of its parts through a nested reference. The report resolves a port reference against the ports of the model the reference reaches into and links the port; where that model is not part of the report, it stays the text the file writes.

datatypes/ReactionFbc.label: ReactionFbc
datatypes/ReactionFbc.summary: what the fbc package adds to a reaction, its flux bounds and its genes
datatypes/ReactionFbc.description:
The report keeps the three things which fbc gives a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) in one block: the [parameters](glossary:types/Parameter) which bound its flux from below and from above, and the [gene product association](glossary:types/GeneProductAssociation) which says under which genes it can run.

The inspector shows the block as three rows of the reaction, [fbc:lowerFluxBound](glossary:types/Reaction/fbc.lowerFluxBound) and [fbc:upperFluxBound](glossary:types/Reaction/fbc.upperFluxBound), each a link to the parameter it names, and [fbc:geneProductAssociation](glossary:types/Reaction/fbc.geneProductAssociation), which names the association and renders its tree below it. The two bounds are columns of the table of the reactions as well.

datatypes/SBOTerm.label: SBOTerm
datatypes/SBOTerm.summary: the identifier of a term of the Systems Biology Ontology
datatypes/SBOTerm.description:
The pattern is fixed: `SBO:` followed by exactly seven digits, for example `SBO:0000014`. The value names a term of the Systems Biology Ontology, a controlled vocabulary of the entities, the roles, the processes and the modelling frameworks a model is built from, and it states in that vocabulary what the class of an element alone does not: that a modifier is a catalyst, that a kinetic law is Michaelis-Menten kinetics, that a parameter is a Michaelis constant. Section 5 of the specification describes how the terms are meant to be used.

The report shows the term in the attributes of the inspector and links it to its page at identifiers.org, where the label and the definition of the term are read.

datatypes/SId.label: SId
datatypes/SId.summary: the identifier of an element inside a model
datatypes/SId.description:
The type of the [id](glossary:types/SBase/id) every element may carry: `SId ::= ( letter | '_' ) idChar*`, where an `idChar` is a letter, a digit or an underscore. The letters are the plain Latin ones, `a` to `z` and `A` to `Z`, so an identifier holds no accent, no space and no dot, and two identifiers are equal only when they match character by character: `S1` and `s1` are two different elements.

An identifier is unique within one model and not within the file, so a reaction and a species of one model cannot share one, while two models of a file may each have a species `S1`. Two further spaces of identifiers sit next to this one: the units of a model, whose identifiers are compared only against each other and against the base units of SBML and which are named by a [UnitSIdRef](glossary:datatypes/UnitSIdRef), and the local parameters of a reaction, whose identifiers are private to that reaction and hide an identifier of the model inside its kinetic law. A package may narrow a space further, as the comp package does for its ports, whose identifiers have to be unique only among the ports of their model.

The report shows the id in the first column of every table, uses it as the label of every link to the element, and builds the [primary key](glossary:concepts/pk) of the element from it.

datatypes/SIdRef.label: SIdRef
datatypes/SIdRef.summary: a reference to an element of the same model by its identifier
datatypes/SIdRef.description:
An attribute of type `SIdRef` holds the [SId](glossary:datatypes/SId) of an element of the model it is written in: the compartment of a species names a compartment, the variable of a rule names the element the rule computes, the conversion factor of a species names a parameter. Which kind of element a given attribute may name is no part of the type but of the attribute, and the entry of the attribute says it. A package may widen where the value is looked up: the references of the comp package which reach into a submodel name an identifier of that submodel and not of the model they are written in, the model reference of a submodel names a model of the document it is written in, and the model reference of an external model definition a model of the document at its source. The value is compared character by character like an identifier, and it has to exist where it is looked up: a reference which ends nowhere is a dangling reference, which makes the file invalid and leaves a simulation without a quantity it needs.

The report resolves every reference of a model against the elements of that model and shows a resolved one as a link to the element it names, while the element at the other end lists the reference under "Referenced by", so that a reference can be followed in both directions. A reference the report cannot resolve stays the text the file writes, without a link.

datatypes/SpeciesFbc.label: SpeciesFbc
datatypes/SpeciesFbc.summary: what the fbc package adds to a species, its composition and its charge
datatypes/SpeciesFbc.description:
The report keeps the two attributes which fbc gives a [species](glossary:types/Species) in one block: the elemental composition of the species and its charge. Neither enters the mathematics of the model, and together they are what a check of the mass and the charge balance of a reaction needs.

The inspector shows the block as two rows of the species, [fbc:chemicalFormula](glossary:types/Species/fbc.chemicalFormula) and [fbc:charge](glossary:types/Species/fbc.charge).

datatypes/UncertKind.label: UncertKind
datatypes/UncertKind.summary: which statistical measure an uncert parameter of an uncertainty is
datatypes/UncertKind.description:
`UncertKind` is derived from [string](glossary:datatypes/string) and holds one of sixteen values, the [type](glossary:types/UncertParameter/type) of an [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter). Ten of them are a single number, which the parameter writes in its [value](glossary:types/UncertParameter/value) or reads from the element its [var](glossary:types/UncertParameter/var) names: the mean, the median, the mode, the variance, the standard deviation, the standard error, the coefficient of variation, the skewness, the kurtosis and the size of the sample. Four of them are an interval and are written as an [uncert span](glossary:types/UncertSpan), with the two ends of the interval in the place of that single number: the range, the confidence interval, the credible interval and the interquartile range. The last two say where a number comes from rather than what it is: `distribution`, the distribution the value was drawn from, and `externalParameter`, a measure this specification does not define, the only value which may be written as either class and the only one which has to carry a [definition](glossary:types/UncertParameter/definitionUrl).

Which attributes and which children a measure may carry follows from its value, and the table of Section 3.11.1 of the specification states it per value: a single number carries units and a value or a var, an interval carries units and its two ends, a distribution carries a definition, math and parameters of its own, and an external parameter may carry all of them. The report shows the value in the first column of the measures of an [uncertainty](glossary:types/Uncertainty) and as the name of a measure which carries no identifier of its own. The sixteen values are:

datatypes/UnitSIdRef.label: UnitSIdRef
datatypes/UnitSIdRef.summary: a reference to a unit by its identifier
datatypes/UnitSIdRef.description:
The identifiers of units live in a space of their own: the id of a [unit definition](glossary:types/UnitDefinition) is of the type `UnitSId`, which has the syntax of an [SId](glossary:datatypes/SId) but is compared only against the other unit identifiers of the model and against the base unit names SBML reserves, `mole`, `litre`, `second`, `kilogram` and the other base units of Table 2 of the specification. An attribute of type `UnitSIdRef`, the units of a compartment, of a parameter or of a species, must name one of the two, a unit definition of the model or a base unit, and anything else is a dangling reference. Because the space is separate from the identifiers of the model, a parameter `volume` and a unit definition `volume` can exist side by side.

The report links a value which names a unit definition to that definition and renders the unit next to the identifier as a formula, the [rendered units](glossary:concepts/unitsLatex); a base unit is no element of the model, so it stays text and only its rendering is added. The units an element ends up with, declared here or inherited from the model, are the [derived units](glossary:concepts/derivedUnits) the report computes on top of this.

datatypes/XHTML.label: XHTML
datatypes/XHTML.summary: a fragment of markup written for human readers
datatypes/XHTML.description:
The [notes](glossary:types/SBase/notes) of an element and the [message](glossary:types/Constraint/message) of a constraint hold XHTML 1.0 in the namespace `http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml`, which is declared either on the content itself, `<body xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">`, or with a prefix on the `sbml` element of the file. The specification asks for no particular element, any well formed XHTML content is allowed, with the single restriction that it carries neither an XML declaration nor a DOCTYPE. This is where the documentation of a published model is written: paragraphs, headings, tables, links to the paper it comes from.

The report renders the markup which notes really use, among it paragraphs, lists, tables, images and links, and drops everything else, so that nothing a file brings with it can act on the page.

datatypes/anyURI.label: anyURI
datatypes/anyURI.summary: a character string which is read as a URI
datatypes/anyURI.description:
The XML Schema type `anyURI` holds a Uniform Resource Identifier as RFC 3986 defines it. That is an address of any of the three shapes such an identifier takes: a URL, `http://example.org/firefly.xml`, a URN, `urn:miriam:biomodels.db:BIOMD0000000002`, or a location relative to the document which writes it, `firefly.xml`. Only the syntax is asked of the value. Whether anything answers at that address, and whether what answers is what was meant, is nothing the file can settle.

The [source](glossary:types/ExternalModelDefinition/source) of an external model definition is of this type, the document which holds the model. The distrib package asks the same of the [definitionURL](glossary:types/UncertParameter/definitionUrl) of an uncertainty parameter and of an [uncert span](glossary:types/UncertSpan/definitionUrl), which names the term an external measure stands for, under the name `ExternalRef`: a string which has to be a valid URI. The report never fetches an address: a relative source is looked for among the entries of the COMBINE archive or among the files next to the document, and every other value is shown as the text the file writes.

datatypes/boolean.label: boolean
datatypes/boolean.summary: a flag which is either true or false
datatypes/boolean.description:
The XML Schema type `boolean` is the type of the flags of SBML: whether a species is [constant](glossary:types/Species/constant), whether a reaction is [reversible](glossary:types/Reaction/reversible), whether an event uses the values of the moment its trigger fired. An attribute writes `true` or `false`, and `1` and `0` are legal spellings of the same two values. In a MathML formula they are not: there `0` and `1` are numbers, and a Boolean value is the element `<true/>` or `<false/>`.

A flag the file leaves out is not the same as a flag set to false, and what an absent flag means is written in the entry of the attribute. The report keeps the two apart: a true flag is a check mark, a false flag a cross, and an attribute the file does not set the dash every empty value of the report shows.

datatypes/double.label: double
datatypes/double.summary: a floating point number, which may be infinite or not a number
datatypes/double.description:
The XML Schema type `double` is the type of every numerical quantity of SBML: the size of a compartment, the initial amount of a species, the value of a parameter, the stoichiometry of a reactant. It is an IEEE 754 double precision number written as a mantissa with an optional exponent, `2`, `-0.3`, `234.234e3`, `6.02E-23`. Its value space holds three values which are no ordinary number: positive infinity, negative infinity and the value which is not a number, written `INF`, `-INF` and `NaN`.

These three are values like any other and say something a reader has to see: the upper flux bound of an unbounded reaction is `INF`, and a `NaN` is a quantity which is declared but whose number is not known. None of them is what an attribute the file leaves out means. The report shows a number with six significant digits and the unrounded value as its tooltip, an infinite value as the sign of infinity with its direction and a `NaN` as itself; [number](glossary:concepts/number) describes the three of them.

datatypes/integer.label: integer
datatypes/integer.description:
Decimal digits with an optional leading sign and nothing after them. The core specification calls this type `int` and holds it to the range of a signed 32 bit number, from -2147483648 to 2147483647; a package may narrow it where it uses a whole number, as the qual package does for the initial level of a [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) and for the result level of a [function term](glossary:types/FunctionTerm), which its specification writes as a non-negative `int`. A whole number is exact and, unlike a [double](glossary:datatypes/double), carries neither a fractional part nor an exponent, which is what makes it the type of a count and of a level.

The report shows a whole number as the file writes it, and what the report counts itself, the number of elements of a [list](glossary:types/ListOf), is a whole number as well.

datatypes/latex.label: latex
datatypes/latex.summary: units the report has rendered as a formula
datatypes/latex.description:
A field of this kind holds the latex of a unit which the page typesets with KaTeX: the units an element declares, resolved from the unit definition it names ([rendered units](glossary:concepts/unitsLatex)), and the units the report derives for an element or for a formula ([derived units](glossary:concepts/derivedUnits)). Both are a product of base units with their exponent, so that millimole over litre is shown as that fraction and not as the identifier `mmol_per_l` a file happens to give it.

A dash stands where a model declares no units and where the report cannot derive any. A units attribute which names `dimensionless` shows its identifier alone, because a quantity without a dimension has no symbol which is shorter than the word.

datatypes/list.label: list
datatypes/list.summary: a field which holds as many values as the element has
datatypes/list.description:
A field of this kind holds every value of an attribute which is not a single one, in the order the file writes them: the species of a model, the reactants of a reaction, the units of a unit definition, the annotations of any element. What the entries are is what the entry of the field says.

Where they are shown depends on the field: the elements of a list of the model are the rows of the table of their type, the elements a list of an element holds are a table in the inspector of that element, and a list without entries is the dash of an empty value. The `listOf` element of the file is not part of what such a field holds: where it states something of its own, a meta id, an SBO term, notes, an annotation, an id or a name, the report keeps it as a [ListOf](glossary:types/ListOf) element of its own, which the element owning the list points at.

datatypes/positiveInteger.label: positiveInteger
datatypes/positiveInteger.summary: a whole number greater than zero
datatypes/positiveInteger.description:
The XML Schema type `positiveInteger` holds 1, 2, 3 and so on, decimal digits with an optional leading plus, and neither zero nor a negative value. XML Schema sets no upper bound on it, but SBML uses the type only where the numbers are small: the [level](glossary:types/SBMLDocument/level) and the [version](glossary:types/SBMLDocument/version) of a file, which say which edition of the language the file is written in, are of this type.

The report shows both in the attributes of the document, which is where reading an unfamiliar file starts.

datatypes/sign.label: sign
datatypes/sign.summary: the direction of the influence an input carries within the system
datatypes/sign.description:
The [sign](glossary:types/Input/sign) of an [input](glossary:types/Input) says whether the contribution of the species it names is positive, negative, both or not known. It is the arrow and the bar of a regulatory network: an activation, an inhibition, an influence which is one or the other depending on the levels of the other regulators, and one the file does not decide. The package defines the type for visualisation: the mathematics of a [transition](glossary:types/Transition) is in its [function terms](glossary:types/FunctionTerm), and the sign has no impact on it.

The report shows the sign next to the species of the input, in the column of the inputs of a transition and in the table of the inputs in the inspector. The four values are:

datatypes/string.label: string
datatypes/string.summary: a sequence of characters with no further restriction
datatypes/string.description:
The XML Schema type `string` holds any finite sequence of characters, every character of Unicode except the two delimiters 0xFFFE and 0xFFFF, and the only further rules are those of XML itself: an ampersand is written `&`, and an apostrophe or a quotation mark which would end the value is written `'` or `"`. Nothing else is asked of it and nothing references it: a string is read by a person, not by the model. The [name](glossary:types/SBase/name) of an element is the string every type carries.

The report shows a string as the text the file writes and a dash where the file writes nothing. Several of the fields the report adds are strings as well, the [equation](glossary:concepts/equation) of a reaction or the XML of an element, and the entry of the field says what they hold.

datatypes/transitionInputEffect.label: transitionInputEffect
datatypes/transitionInputEffect.summary: what a transition does to the level of a species it reads
datatypes/transitionInputEffect.description:
The [transition effect](glossary:types/Input/transitionEffect) of an [input](glossary:types/Input) tells a read from a consumption. With `none` the level of the species is not modified by the [transition](glossary:types/Transition), which is what a logical model writes and what a read arc of a Petri net is. With `consumption` the level is decreased by the [result level](glossary:types/FunctionTerm/resultLevel) of the term which applies, multiplied by the [threshold level](glossary:types/Input/thresholdLevel) of the input where it sets one, which is how a Petri net takes the tokens of the place before a transition away.

A species which is [constant](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies/constant) may only be read, so an input of such a species cannot be consumed. The report shows the effect in the table of the inputs in the inspector of the transition. The two values are:

datatypes/transitionOutputEffect.label: transitionOutputEffect
datatypes/transitionOutputEffect.summary: whether a transition adds to the level of a species it changes or sets it
datatypes/transitionOutputEffect.description:
The [transition effect](glossary:types/Output/transitionEffect) of an [output](glossary:types/Output) is the attribute which says in which of the two formalisms of the package a file is written. With `production` the level of the species is increased by the [result level](glossary:types/FunctionTerm/resultLevel) of the term which applies, multiplied by the [output level](glossary:types/Output/outputLevel) of the output, which is the weight of the arc of a Petri net; an output of this effect has to state its output level, because SBML Level 3 has no default values. With `assignmentLevel` the level of the species becomes that result level, which is how a logical model assigns the value of its rule, and the output level has no meaning.

The report shows the effect in the table of the outputs in the inspector of the transition. The two values are:

links/activeObjective.label: activeObjective
links/activeObjective.summary: the objective a model declares as the one which is optimised
links/activeObjective.description:
A [model](glossary:types/Model) which defines several [objectives](glossary:types/Objective) names the one an analysis optimises unless it is told otherwise. It is the only link which starts at the model itself, because the attribute belongs to the list of the objectives, which the report shows as the section of that type.

It is shown under "References" of the model and under "Referenced by" of the objective, where it says that this objective is the one the model was published with.

links/associatedSpecies.label: associatedSpecies
links/associatedSpecies.summary: the species a gene product stands for
links/associatedSpecies.description:
A [gene product](glossary:types/GeneProduct) may name the [species](glossary:types/Species) which represents it in the reaction network, which is how some reconstructions encode gene products.

The link is shown under "References" of the gene product and under "Referenced by" of the species.

links/coefficient.label: coefficient
links/coefficient.summary: the parameter which holds the weight of a term
links/coefficient.description:
A [component](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent) of a user defined constraint does not write its weight into the file: it names the [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) which holds it, so that the weights of a model are changed in one place.

It is shown under "References" of the component and under "Referenced by" of the parameter, where it says which constraints a number belongs to.

links/compartment.label: compartment
links/compartment.summary: the compartment a species or a qualitative species is located in, or a reaction takes place in
links/compartment.description:
Every [species](glossary:types/Species) and every [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) names the compartment it is located in, and a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) may name the compartment it takes place in.

The link is shown under "References" of the species, of the qualitative species or of the reaction, and under "Referenced by" of the compartment, which is where every species of a compartment can be seen at once.

links/constraintComponent.label: constraintComponent
links/constraintComponent.summary: a term of a user defined constraint
links/constraintComponent.description:
A [user defined constraint](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraint) names every [component](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent) it is the sum of, the way a reaction names its species references, and each component names the variable it weighs and the parameter of its coefficient with links of their own.

It is shown under "References" of the constraint and under "Referenced by" of the component.

links/conversionFactor.label: conversionFactor
links/conversionFactor.summary: the parameter which converts the values of an element
links/conversionFactor.description:
A [model](glossary:types/Model) and a [species](glossary:types/Species) name a conversion factor parameter for the amounts of species, and a [replaced element](glossary:types/ReplacedElement) names one for the element it replaces. In every case the link goes to a constant [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) of the model. The two conversion factors of a [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) are links of their own, [time conversion factor](glossary:links/timeConversionFactor) and [extent conversion factor](glossary:links/extentConversionFactor).

It is shown under "References" of the element and under "Referenced by" of the parameter.

links/defaultTerm.label: defaultTerm
links/defaultTerm.summary: the term of a transition which holds where no other one does
links/defaultTerm.description:
A [transition](glossary:types/Transition) has exactly one [default term](glossary:types/DefaultTerm), which gives the level of every state its function terms do not cover. It is a link of its own and not a function term link, because the term carries no condition and is the last row of the transition table whatever the order of the others.

It is shown under "References" of the transition and under "Referenced by" of the term.

links/delay.label: delay
links/delay.summary: the formula which postpones the execution of an event
links/delay.description:
An [event](glossary:types/Event) may hold a [delay](glossary:types/Delay) of its own, and the link runs from the event to it.

It is shown under "References" of the event and under "Referenced by" of the delay.

links/deletion.label: deletion
links/deletion.summary: an element which a submodel removes, and the deletion which removes it
links/deletion.description:
A [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) names every [deletion](glossary:types/Deletion) it carries, and each deletion names the element of the instantiated model which it removes, so the link leads from the submodel over the deletion to the element which the composed model does not contain. The same kind leads from a [replaced element](glossary:types/ReplacedElement) to the deletion it stands for, which is how a model records that an element of its own takes the place of something a submodel lost.

Where the model of the submodel is one of another document, the link ends at the element of [that document](glossary:concepts/targetEntry) when it is part of the report, as another entry of the same archive. When it is not, the deletion has no element to name and the link ends at the deletion.

The link is shown under "References" of the submodel and of the deletion, and under "Referenced by" of the element which is removed.

links/eventAssignment.label: eventAssignment
links/eventAssignment.summary: a new value an event gives to an element of the model
links/eventAssignment.description:
An [event](glossary:types/Event) names every [event assignment](glossary:types/EventAssignment) of its list, and each assignment names the element it sets with a [variable](glossary:links/variable) link and the elements its formula reads with [math](glossary:links/math) links. An assignment carries no identifier in most models, so this link is what says which event it belongs to.

It is shown under "References" of the event and under "Referenced by" of the assignment.

links/extentConversionFactor.label: extentConversionFactor
links/extentConversionFactor.summary: the parameter which converts the reaction extent of a submodel
links/extentConversionFactor.description:
A [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) names the [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) which converts the units of reaction extent of the model it instantiates into those of the model which contains it, in its [extent conversion factor](glossary:types/Submodel/extentConversionFactor).

It is shown under "References" of the submodel and under "Referenced by" of the parameter.

links/externalModelDefinition.label: externalModelDefinition
links/externalModelDefinition.summary: a model of another document which this document refers to
links/externalModelDefinition.description:
The [document](glossary:types/SBMLDocument) names every [external model definition](glossary:types/ExternalModelDefinition) of its list. The model behind it lives in another file, which the report follows where it has that file, and a [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) instantiates it with a [model reference](glossary:links/modelRef) link.

It is shown under "References" of the document and under "Referenced by" of the external model definition.

links/fluxBound.label: fluxBound
links/fluxBound.summary: the reaction a flux bound of fbc Version 1 constrains
links/fluxBound.description:
In a document of fbc Version 1 a [flux bound](glossary:types/FluxBound) is an object of its own, which names the [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) whose flux it constrains together with an operation and a value. From Version 2 on the bounds are attributes of the reaction, which names their parameters with a [lower flux bound](glossary:links/lowerFluxBound) and an [upper flux bound](glossary:links/upperFluxBound) link.

The link is shown under "References" of the flux bound and under "Referenced by" of the reaction, where it shows what bounds its flux.

links/fluxObjective.label: fluxObjective
links/fluxObjective.summary: a term of an objective function and the reaction whose flux it weighs
links/fluxObjective.description:
An [objective](glossary:types/Objective) names every [flux objective](glossary:types/FluxObjective) it is the sum of, and each of those names the [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) whose flux it weighs. Both hops carry this kind, the way a reaction and its species reference both carry the kind of the participation. From Version 3 of fbc on a quadratic term may multiply the flux with the flux of a second reaction, which is a link of its own, [second reaction](glossary:links/reaction2).

The coefficient is an attribute of the flux objective, not of the link. The chain is shown under "References" of the objective and of the flux objective, and under "Referenced by" of the reaction, where it says that this reaction is what the model optimises.

links/functionTerm.label: functionTerm
links/functionTerm.summary: a row of the transition table of a transition
links/functionTerm.description:
A [transition](glossary:types/Transition) names every [function term](glossary:types/FunctionTerm) of its list, in the order in which they are read, and the math of a term reaches the qualitative species, the inputs and the outputs it names with [math](glossary:links/math) links of its own.

It is shown under "References" of the transition and under "Referenced by" of the term. The terms are the rows of the table of their transition, so the other links look across them, the way they look across the kinetic law of a reaction: the transition lists what its conditions read under "math", and a qualitative species a condition reads lists the transition there. A term keeps its own links.

links/geneProduct.label: geneProduct
links/geneProduct.summary: a gene product a reaction needs, named by a reference of its association
links/geneProduct.description:
The link goes from a [gene product reference](glossary:types/GeneProductRef), the leaf of the gene product association of a reaction, to the [gene product](glossary:types/GeneProduct) it names. It starts at the reference and not at the [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) because that is where the file writes the identifier, and because a reaction may name one gene in several branches of its association.

It is shown under "References" of the reference and under "Referenced by" of the gene product. The inspector looks across the tree of the association, which is the question a reader asks: a reaction lists the gene products it needs under this kind, and a gene product lists the reactions which need it, each of them once.

links/geneProductAssociation.label: geneProductAssociation
links/geneProductAssociation.summary: a node of the gene association of a reaction, from the reaction down to its genes
links/geneProductAssociation.description:
A [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) names the [gene product association](glossary:types/GeneProductAssociation) it carries, the association names the node at the root of its tree, and every [and](glossary:types/And) and [or](glossary:types/Or) names the nodes below it, all of them with this kind. The tree ends at the [gene product references](glossary:types/GeneProductRef), which name the genes.

The chain is what makes the structure of the association walkable: it says which genes belong to the same complex and which of them are alternatives, which the flat list of the genes of a reaction cannot.

It is shown under "References" of the reaction and of every node, and under "Referenced by" of the node below.

links/input.label: input
links/input.summary: a qualitative species a transition reads
links/input.description:
A [transition](glossary:types/Transition) names every [input](glossary:types/Input) it lists and each input names the [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) whose level it reads, the way a reaction names its species references. The [sign](glossary:types/Input/sign) of the input says whether that species activates or inhibits, so the inputs and the [outputs](glossary:links/output) of a model together are its influence graph.

It is shown under "References" of the transition and of the input and under "Referenced by" of the qualitative species, where it says which transitions read it.

links/kineticLaw.label: kineticLaw
links/kineticLaw.summary: the formula which gives the speed of a reaction
links/kineticLaw.description:
A [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) holds the formula of its speed in a [kinetic law](glossary:types/KineticLaw) of its own, and the link runs from the reaction to it. The elements the formula reads are linked from the kinetic law with [math](glossary:links/math) links, and its local parameters are among them.

It is shown under "References" of the reaction and under "Referenced by" of the kinetic law. A reaction has one kinetic law at most, and its formula is the speed of the reaction, so the other links look across it: the reaction lists what its formula reads under "math", and a species or a parameter the formula reads lists the reaction there, not the kinetic law. The kinetic law keeps its own links.

links/listOf.label: listOf
links/listOf.summary: a list of the element which states something of its own
links/listOf.description:
An element names every [list](glossary:types/ListOf) it owns which carries a meta id, an SBO term, notes, an annotation, an id or a name: a model its `listOfSpecies`, a reaction its `listOfReactants`, a unit definition its `listOfUnits`. A list which states nothing is no element of the report and has no link. A [port](glossary:types/Port), a [deletion](glossary:types/Deletion) or a replacement of the comp package which names a list by its meta id or its id ends at the list with a link of its own kind.

It is shown under "References" of the element which owns the list and under "Referenced by" of the list, which is how a reader gets from a list back to its owner.

links/localParameter.label: localParameter
links/localParameter.summary: a parameter which only the formula of one kinetic law can read
links/localParameter.description:
A [kinetic law](glossary:types/KineticLaw) names every [local parameter](glossary:types/LocalParameter) it lists, whether its formula reads it or not. A local parameter is not part of the identifiers of the model, only the formula of its own kinetic law can name it, so this link is what says which reaction a local parameter belongs to.

It is shown under "References" of the kinetic law and under "Referenced by" of the local parameter.

links/lowerBound.label: lowerBound
links/lowerBound.summary: the parameter which holds the lowest value of a user defined constraint
links/lowerBound.description:
A [user defined constraint](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraint) keeps the weighted sum of its components between two numbers, and it names the [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) of the lower one in its [lower bound](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraint/lowerBound). The bound limits the sum and not the flux of one reaction, which is why it is not a flux bound.

It is shown under "References" of the constraint and under "Referenced by" of the parameter.

links/lowerFluxBound.label: lowerFluxBound
links/lowerFluxBound.summary: the parameter which holds the lowest flux of a reaction
links/lowerFluxBound.description:
A [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) of a model which uses fbc Version 2 or later names the [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) of its [lower flux bound](glossary:types/Reaction/fbc.lowerFluxBound). A genome scale model gives hundreds of reactions the same parameter, and the link says of every one of them that it is their lower bound.

It is shown under "References" of the reaction and under "Referenced by" of the parameter.

links/math.label: math
links/math.summary: an element a formula refers to
links/math.description:
Every formula of a model refers to elements by their identifier: the species and the parameters of a kinetic law, the elements a rule or a trigger reads, the function definition a formula calls. The report collects these symbols of every formula and links each of them to the element it names, resolving the local parameters of a kinetic law before the elements of the model. The arguments of a function definition are local to it and are no references, and a symbol which names nothing, such as the symbol of time, produces no link.

The link is shown under "References" of the element which carries the formula and under "Referenced by" of the element the formula uses, where it answers in which equations a species or a parameter occurs. The formula of a [kinetic law](glossary:links/kineticLaw) is the speed of its reaction and the condition of a [function term](glossary:links/functionTerm) a row of the table of its transition, so their links are shown as those of the reaction and of the transition, and the kinetic law and the term keep their own.

links/model.label: model
links/model.description:
The [document](glossary:types/SBMLDocument) names the [model](glossary:types/Model) it holds and, in a document of the comp package, every model definition of its list, which are models a submodel can instantiate. A model definition which no submodel instantiates is still reached from the document.

It is shown under "References" of the document and under "Referenced by" of the model.

links/modelRef.label: modelRef
links/modelRef.description:
A [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) names the model it instantiates, which is either a [model](glossary:types/Model) definition of the document or an [external model definition](glossary:types/ExternalModelDefinition). The reference is resolved against the models of the document, not within one model, because model identifiers live in a namespace of the document. An external model definition names a model in turn, the one of another document, and carries the same link to it where the report has that document.

The link is shown under "References" of the submodel and under "Referenced by" of the model, where it shows who uses it.

links/modifier.label: modifier
links/modifier.summary: a species which influences a reaction without being consumed
links/modifier.description:
The link is two links of one kind: from the [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) to every [modifier species reference](glossary:types/ModifierSpeciesReference) of its list of modifiers, and from each of those to the [species](glossary:types/Species) it names: a catalyst, an inhibitor or an activator.

It is shown under "References" of the reaction and under "Referenced by" of the species. A species which is a modifier of a reaction usually also appears in the math of its kinetic law, which is a link of the kind "math".

links/output.label: output
links/output.summary: a qualitative species a transition changes
links/output.description:
A [transition](glossary:types/Transition) names every [output](glossary:types/Output) it lists and each output names the [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) whose level it changes.

It is shown under "References" of the transition and of the output and under "Referenced by" of the qualitative species, where it says which transitions decide its level.

links/port.label: port
links/port.description:
A [port](glossary:types/Port) names exactly one element of its model, by its identifier, by the identifier of a unit definition or by its meta id. All three produce a link of this kind; a port which names a port of a submodel instead is not resolved, because the element lies inside another model.

The link is shown under "References" of the port and under "Referenced by" of the element, where it says that the element is part of the interface of the model.

links/priority.label: priority
links/priority.summary: the formula which orders an event against the events of the same moment
links/priority.description:
An [event](glossary:types/Event) may hold a [priority](glossary:types/Priority) of its own, and the link runs from the event to it.

It is shown under "References" of the event and under "Referenced by" of the priority.

links/product.label: product
links/product.description:
The link is two links of one kind: from the [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) to every [species reference](glossary:types/SpeciesReference) of its list of products, and from each of those to the [species](glossary:types/Species) it names.

It is shown under "References" of the reaction and under "Referenced by" of the species, where it answers which reactions produce it.

links/reactant.label: reactant
links/reactant.description:
The link is two links of one kind: from the [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) to every [species reference](glossary:types/SpeciesReference) of its list of reactants, and from each of those to the [species](glossary:types/Species) it names. Every link starts at the element which carries the reference, so a species reference is part of the graph instead of standing alone.

It is shown under "References" of the reaction, where it lists what the reaction consumes, and under "Referenced by" of the species, where it answers which reactions consume it.

links/reaction2.label: reaction2
links/reaction2.summary: the second flux of a quadratic term of an objective
links/reaction2.description:
A quadratic [flux objective](glossary:types/FluxObjective) of fbc Version 3 weighs the product of the flux of its reaction and the flux of its [second reaction](glossary:types/FluxObjective/reaction2). The second one has a link of its own, so that the reaction it names says that it is the second factor of a product and not a term of the objective of its own.

It is shown under "References" of the flux objective and under "Referenced by" of the reaction.

links/replacedBy.label: replacedBy
links/replacedBy.summary: the element of a submodel which replaces this one
links/replacedBy.description:
An element which is replaced names the [replacement](glossary:types/ReplacedBy) it carries, and the replacement names the element of the [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) which takes the place of the element, so the link leads from the replaced element over the replacement to the element which stays in the composed model.

Where the model of the submodel is one of another document, the link ends at the element of [that document](glossary:concepts/targetEntry) when it is part of the report. Where the reference cannot be resolved, because the report does not have the document of an external model or because the named element is not part of it, the link ends at the submodel, which is as far as the report can follow it.

The link is shown under "References" of the replaced element and of the replacement, and under "Referenced by" of the element which replaces it.

links/replacedElement.label: replacedElement
links/replacedElement.summary: the element of a submodel which this one replaces
links/replacedElement.description:
An element may replace elements of submodels. It names every [replacement](glossary:types/ReplacedElement) it carries, and each replacement names the [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) it reaches into and the element inside it which disappears from the composed model. It is the opposite direction of "replaced by" and the usual way a composed model connects its parts.

Where the model of the submodel is one of another document, the link ends at the element of [that document](glossary:concepts/targetEntry) when it is part of the report. Where the reference cannot be resolved, because the report does not have the document of an external model or because the named element is not part of it, the link ends at the submodel.

The link is shown under "References" of the replacing element and of the replacement, and under "Referenced by" of the element which is replaced.

links/sBaseRef.label: sBaseRef
links/sBaseRef.summary: the next link of a chain of references into a submodel of a submodel
links/sBaseRef.description:
A [port](glossary:types/Port), a [deletion](glossary:types/Deletion), a [replaced element](glossary:types/ReplacedElement) or a [replaced by](glossary:types/ReplacedBy) which has to reach an element deeper than the submodel it names carries a [reference](glossary:types/SBaseRef) of its own, and that reference may carry the next one. Each of them names the reference it carries. The element at the end of the chain is linked from the object which carries the whole chain, so the links in between only say where they belong.

It is shown under "References" of the object which carries the reference and under "Referenced by" of the reference.

links/symbol.label: symbol
links/symbol.summary: the element whose initial value an initial assignment computes
links/symbol.description:
An [initial assignment](glossary:types/InitialAssignment) names the element it computes in its symbol. It is the same relation as the variable of a rule, at the start of the simulation instead of during it, and the specification gives it a name of its own.

The link is shown under "References" of the initial assignment and under "Referenced by" of the element.

links/timeConversionFactor.label: timeConversionFactor
links/timeConversionFactor.summary: the parameter which converts the time of a submodel
links/timeConversionFactor.description:
A [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) names the [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) which converts the units of time of the model it instantiates into the units of time of the model which contains it, in its [time conversion factor](glossary:types/Submodel/timeConversionFactor).

It is shown under "References" of the submodel and under "Referenced by" of the parameter.

links/trigger.label: trigger
links/trigger.summary: the condition an event fires on
links/trigger.description:
An [event](glossary:types/Event) holds its condition in a [trigger](glossary:types/Trigger) of its own, and the link runs from the event to it. The elements the condition reads are linked from the trigger, not from the event, so a reader sees which of the formulas of an event uses a species or a parameter.

It is shown under "References" of the event and under "Referenced by" of the trigger.

links/uncertParameter.label: uncertParameter
links/uncertParameter.description:
An [uncertainty](glossary:types/Uncertainty) names every [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter) it lists, and a parameter of the type `distribution` or `externalParameter` names the parameters which define it in turn, so the link carries the whole tree of a distribution.

It is shown under "References" of the uncertainty and of a parameter with parameters of its own, and under "Referenced by" of the measure, which is how a reader gets from a measure back to the set it belongs to.

links/uncertainty.label: uncertainty
links/uncertainty.summary: a set of measures of how well the value of an element is known
links/uncertainty.description:
An element whose value is uncertain names every [uncertainty](glossary:types/Uncertainty) it carries, and each uncertainty names the [uncert parameters](glossary:types/UncertParameter) which are its measures with [uncert parameter](glossary:links/uncertParameter) links. An element may carry several uncertainties, one per experiment or publication, so the link is what says which element a set of measures describes.

It is shown under "References" of the element and under "Referenced by" of the uncertainty, which is how a reader gets from an uncertainty back to the value it is about.

links/units.label: units
links/units.summary: the unit definition an element declares its units with
links/units.description:
A [model](glossary:types/Model), a [compartment](glossary:types/Compartment), a [species](glossary:types/Species), a [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter), a [local parameter](glossary:types/LocalParameter) and an [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter) may name a [unit definition](glossary:types/UnitDefinition) of the model in one of their units attributes. A units attribute which names a base unit of SBML instead of a unit definition produces no link, because there is no element to link to.

Two more references carry the same relation. A number in a formula of Level 3 may name its units with the attribute `sbml:units`, and the element which holds the formula links that unit definition. A model of Level 1 or Level 2 changes the units every element without units of its own uses by defining a unit of the id `substance`, `time`, `volume`, `area` or `length`, and the model links such a definition, the way a model of Level 3 links the unit definitions of its units attributes.

The link is shown under "References" of the element and under "Referenced by" of the unit definition, where it shows which elements are measured in it.

links/upperBound.label: upperBound
links/upperBound.summary: the parameter which holds the highest value of a user defined constraint
links/upperBound.description:
A [user defined constraint](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraint) keeps the weighted sum of its components between two numbers, and it names the [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) of the upper one in its [upper bound](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraint/upperBound). The bound limits the sum and not the flux of one reaction, which is why it is not a flux bound.

It is shown under "References" of the constraint and under "Referenced by" of the parameter.

links/upperFluxBound.label: upperFluxBound
links/upperFluxBound.summary: the parameter which holds the highest flux of a reaction
links/upperFluxBound.description:
A [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) of a model which uses fbc Version 2 or later names the [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) of its [upper flux bound](glossary:types/Reaction/fbc.upperFluxBound). A genome scale model gives hundreds of reactions the same parameter, and the link says of every one of them that it is their upper bound.

It is shown under "References" of the reaction and under "Referenced by" of the parameter.

links/var.label: var
links/var.summary: the element which holds the number of a measure
links/var.description:
A measure of an [uncertainty](glossary:types/Uncertainty) which is not a fixed number names the element of the model which holds it in the [var](glossary:types/UncertParameter/var) of an [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter). The two ends of the interval of an [uncert span](glossary:types/UncertSpan) are links of their own, [var lower](glossary:links/varLower) and [var upper](glossary:links/varUpper).

It is shown under "References" of the measure and under "Referenced by" of the element it names, where it says which measurement that element stands for.

links/varLower.label: varLower
links/varLower.summary: the element which holds the lower end of the interval of a measure
links/varLower.description:
An [uncert span](glossary:types/UncertSpan) whose lower end is not a fixed number names the element of the model which holds it in its [var lower](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varLower). The link says of that element that it is the lower end of the interval, which the element does not say itself.

It is shown under "References" of the span and under "Referenced by" of the element it names.

links/varUpper.label: varUpper
links/varUpper.summary: the element which holds the upper end of the interval of a measure
links/varUpper.description:
An [uncert span](glossary:types/UncertSpan) whose upper end is not a fixed number names the element of the model which holds it in its [var upper](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varUpper). The link says of that element that it is the upper end of the interval, which the element does not say itself.

It is shown under "References" of the span and under "Referenced by" of the element it names.

links/variable.label: variable
links/variable.summary: the element a rule, an event assignment or a constraint component is about
links/variable.description:
An [assignment rule](glossary:types/AssignmentRule), a [rate rule](glossary:types/RateRule) and an [event assignment](glossary:types/EventAssignment) name the element they set in their variable: a compartment, a species, a parameter or the stoichiometry of a species reference. A [component](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent) of a user defined constraint of fbc names the reaction or the parameter it weighs with the same attribute, which it does not set but reads; the second factor of a quadratic component is a link of its own, [second variable](glossary:links/variable2).

The link is shown under "References" of the rule or of the assignment, and under "Referenced by" of the element, where it shows what determines its value.

links/variable2.label: variable2
links/variable2.summary: the second factor of a quadratic term of a user defined constraint
links/variable2.description:
A quadratic [component](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent) of a user defined constraint weighs the product of two variables, the reaction or the parameter of its [variable](glossary:links/variable) and the one of its [second variable](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/variable2). The second one has a link of its own, so that the element it names says that it is the second factor of a product and not a term of its own.

It is shown under "References" of the component and under "Referenced by" of the reaction or the parameter.

types/AlgebraicRule.label: AlgebraicRule
types/AlgebraicRule.summary: an equation which has to hold at every moment of the simulation
types/AlgebraicRule.description:
An algebraic rule states that an expression is zero: `0 = f(W)`. It constrains the elements of the model without saying which of them it determines, which is why a simulator has to solve it together with the rest of the system. A model must not be overdetermined, so at least one element of the equation has to be free, that is not constant and not determined by another rule or by the reactions.

The report shows the rendered equation and the units it produces; which element it determines follows from the rest of the model.

rules.message: The system of equations created from an SBML model must not be overdetermined.

The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on a rule is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to a mathematical expression (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000064, "mathematical expression"). Note: This applies to Algebraic Rules in addition to Rate and Assignment Rules.
An AlgebraicRule object may have the optional attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on an AlgebraicRule object.

types/AlgebraicRule/derivedUnits.label: derived units
types/AlgebraicRule/derivedUnits.summary: the units of the expression as the report derives them
types/AlgebraicRule/derivedUnits.description: The report derives the units of the expression from the units of the quantities it uses. The terms of an equation should all have the same units.

types/AlgebraicRule/math.label: math
types/AlgebraicRule/math.summary: the expression which has to be zero
types/AlgebraicRule/math.description:
The math is an arbitrary expression which returns a number, and the rule says that this number is zero at all times.

The report renders the expression in the column "math" and in the inspector.
types/AlgebraicRule/math.default: how the rule behaves mathematically stays undefined

rules.message: Every AssignmentRule, RateRule and AlgebraicRule object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/And.label: And
types/And.summary: the associations below it are all needed at once
types/And.description:
An `and` is a complex: every gene below it has to be expressed for the reaction to run, and the loss of one of them stops the reaction. It holds two or more nodes, each of which is an [and](glossary:types/And), an [or](glossary:types/Or) or a [gene product reference](glossary:types/GeneProductRef), so the operators nest to any depth.

The report shows it as the branches of the tree in the inspector of a reaction and links the nodes below it.

rules.message: An <And> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on an <GeneAnd.
An <And> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on an <And>.

An <And> object must have two or more concrete <Association> objects: <GeneProductRef>, <And>, or <Or>. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespace are permitted on an <And> object.

types/And/associations.label: associations
types/And/associations.summary: the nodes which are all needed, two or more of them
types/And/associations.description: The order of the nodes carries no meaning: an `and` is a set of conditions which hold at the same time. The report keeps them in the order of the file.

rules.message: An <And> object must have two or more concrete <Association> objects: <GeneProductRef>, <And>, or <Or>. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespace are permitted on an <And> object.

types/AssignmentRule.label: AssignmentRule
types/AssignmentRule.summary: a formula which holds at every moment of the simulation
types/AssignmentRule.description:
An assignment rule states that a variable of the model equals an expression, at all times, and not only at the start: `x = f(V)`.
