It is the way to define a quantity which follows from others, for example a total concentration or a saturation. The element it assigns to must not be constant, and no other rule may assign to the same element.

The report shows the variable, the rendered formula and the units the formula produces.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on a rule is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to a mathematical expression (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000064, "mathematical expression"). Note: This applies to Algebraic Rules in addition to Rate and Assignment Rules.

There must not be circular dependencies in the combined set of <initialAssignment>, <assignmentRule> and <kineticLaw> definitions in a model. Each of these constructs has the effect of assigning a value to an identifier (i.e. the identifier given in the field 'symbol' in <initialAssignment>, the field 'variable' in <assignmentRule>, and the field 'id' on the <kineticLaw>'s enclosing <reaction>). Each of these constructs computes the value using a mathematical formula. The formula for a given identifier cannot make reference to a second identifier whose own definition depends directly or indirectly on the first identifier.

An AssignmentRule object must have the required attribute 'variable' and may have the optional attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on an AssignmentRule object.

types/AssignmentRule/derivedUnits.label: derived units
types/AssignmentRule/derivedUnits.summary: the units of the formula as the report derives them
types/AssignmentRule/derivedUnits.description: The report derives the units of the formula from the units of the quantities it uses. They should be the units of the variable the rule assigns to.

types/AssignmentRule/math.label: math
types/AssignmentRule/math.summary: the formula which computes the value of the variable
types/AssignmentRule/math.description:
The math is an arbitrary expression which returns a number. Its units should be the units of the variable.

The report renders the formula in the column "math" and in the inspector.
types/AssignmentRule/math.default: how the rule behaves mathematically stays undefined

rules.message: Every AssignmentRule, RateRule and AlgebraicRule object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/AssignmentRule/variable.label: variable
types/AssignmentRule/variable.summary: the element the rule assigns to
types/AssignmentRule/variable.description:
The variable names the compartment, species, species reference or parameter whose value the rule determines. It must not be constant, and a model may not contain a second rule for the same variable.

The report links the named element in the column "variable" and in the inspector.

rules.message: The value of the 'variable' field in all <assignmentRule> and <rateRule> definitions must be unique across the set of all such rule definitions in a model.

The value of an <assignmentRule>'s 'variable' must be the identifier of an existing <compartment>, <species>, globally-defined <parameter>, or (in Level 3) <speciesReference>, or (in Level 3 Version 2), any identifier in the SId namespace of the model belonging to an element defined by an SBML Level 3 package as having with mathematical meaning.

Any <compartment>, <species>, <parameter>, or (in Level 3) <speciesReference> whose identifier is the value of a 'variable' attribute in an <assignmentRule>, must have a value of 'false' for 'constant'.
The value of a <rateRule> or <assignmentRule>'s 'variable' attribute must not be the identifier of a <compartment> with a 'spatialDimensions' value of 0.

types/Compartment.label: Compartment
types/Compartment.summary: a bounded space in which species are located
types/Compartment.description:
A compartment is the place where something is: a cell, an organelle, a membrane, the extracellular space. Every species of a model has to be located in one, which is why a model with species always has at least one compartment. A compartment does not have to correspond to a physical structure, it is whatever the model treats as one well mixed space.

The report shows the size of a compartment, the units of that size and the units it derives, and links the species which are located in it.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on a <compartment> is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/). In SBML Level 2 prior to Version 4 it is expected to refer to a participant physical type (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000236, "participant physical type"); in Versions 4 and above it is expected to refer to a material entity (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000240, "material entity").

A Compartment object must have the required attributes 'id' and 'constant', and may have the optional attributes 'metaid', 'sboTerm', 'name', 'spatialDimensions', 'size' and 'units'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a Compartment object.

types/Compartment/constant.label: constant
types/Compartment/constant.summary: whether the size of the compartment stays fixed during a simulation
types/Compartment/constant.description:
A constant compartment keeps its size for the whole simulation and can only be given a value by an initial assignment. A compartment which is not constant can be changed by a rule or by an event, which is how a growing cell is modelled.

The report shows the flag as a mark in the column "constant".

rules.message: If a <compartment> definition has a 'spatialDimensions' value of '0', then its 'constant' attribute value must either default to or be set to 'true'. If the compartment has no dimensions, then its size can never change.

types/Compartment/derivedUnits.label: derived units
types/Compartment/derivedUnits.summary: the units of the size as the report derives them
types/Compartment/derivedUnits.description: The report derives the units of a compartment from its own units, or from the units of the model which it inherits, and renders them as a formula. Derived units make it visible what a value means even when the model does not declare units everywhere.

types/Compartment/size.label: size
types/Compartment/size.summary: the size of the compartment at the start of the simulation
types/Compartment/size.description:
The size is the volume, the area or the length of the compartment, depending on its dimensions. It is optional: a missing size means that the value is unknown or that it is computed by an initial assignment or a rule, it does not mean one. When the compartment is not constant, the size can change during a simulation.

The report shows the size in the table and in the inspector, and the identifier of a compartment stands for its size in every formula of the model.
types/Compartment/size.default: the size is unknown or set by an initial assignment or a rule

rules.message: The size of a <compartment> must not be set if the compartment's 'spatialDimensions' attribute has value '0'.

As a principle of best modeling practice, the size of a <compartment> should be set to a value rather than be left undefined. Doing so improves the portability of models between different simulation and analysis systems, and helps make it easier to detect potential errors in models.

types/Compartment/spatialDimensions.label: spatialDimensions
types/Compartment/spatialDimensions.summary: the number of dimensions of the compartment
types/Compartment/spatialDimensions.description:
Three dimensions means the size is a volume, two means an area, one means a length. The value does not enter the mathematics of the model, but it decides which units of the model a compartment inherits when it does not declare its own.

The report shows the dimensions in the column "dimensions" and in the inspector.
types/Compartment/spatialDimensions.default: no units are inherited from the model, because there is no basis to choose between volume, area and length

rules.message: If neither the attribute 'units' nor the attribute 'spatialDimensions' on a Compartment object is set, the unit associated with that compartment's size is undefined.

types/Compartment/units.label: units
types/Compartment/units.summary: the units of the size of the compartment
types/Compartment/units.description:
The units are either a unit definition of the model or one of the base units. When they are not declared, the compartment inherits the volume, area or length units of the model according to its dimensions, and when the model does not declare those either, the size has no units.

The report links the referenced unit definition and renders it as a formula.
types/Compartment/units.default: the volume, area or length units of the model, according to the dimensions of the compartment

rules.message: The syntax of unit identifiers (i.e., the values of the 'id' attribute on UnitDefinition, the 'units' attribute on Compartment, the 'units' attribute on Parameter, and the 'substanceUnits' attribute on Species) must conform to the syntax of the SBML type UnitSId.

Unit identifier references (i.e the 'units' attribute on <Compartment>, the 'units' attribute on <Parameter>, and the 'substanceUnits' attribute on <Species>) must be the identifier of a <UnitDefinition> in the <Model>, or the identifier of a predefined unit in SBML.

If a <compartment> definition has a 'spatialDimensions' value of '0', then its 'units' attribute must not be set. If the compartment has no dimensions, then no units can be associated with a non-existent size.

If the attribute 'units' on a Compartment object having a 'spatialDimensions' attribute value of '1' has not been set, then the unit of measurement associated with the compartment's size is determined by the value of the enclosing Model object's 'lengthUnits' attribute. If neither the Compartment object's 'units' nor the enclosing Model object's 'lengthUnits' attributes are set, the unit of compartment size is undefined.

If the attribute 'units' on a Compartment object having a 'spatialDimensions' attribute value of '2' has not been set, then the unit of measurement associated with the compartment's size is determined by the value of the enclosing Model object's 'areaUnits' attribute. If neither the Compartment object's 'units' nor the enclosing Model object's 'areaUnits' attributes are set, the unit of compartment size is undefined.

If the attribute 'units' on a Compartment object having a 'spatialDimensions' attribute value of '3' has not been set, then the unit of measurement associated with the compartment's size is determined by the value of the enclosing Model object's 'volumeUnits' attribute. If neither the Compartment object's 'units' nor the enclosing Model object's 'volumeUnits' attributes are set, the unit of compartment size is undefined.
If neither the attribute 'units' nor the attribute 'spatialDimensions' on a Compartment object is set, the unit associated with that compartment's size is undefined.

types/Compartment/unitsLatex.label: rendered units
types/Compartment/unitsLatex.summary: the units of the size rendered as a formula
types/Compartment/unitsLatex.description: The report resolves the unit definition the compartment references and renders it as a formula, so that the table shows the unit itself and not only its identifier.

types/Constraint.label: Constraint
types/Constraint.summary: a condition which a valid simulation of the model has to satisfy
types/Constraint.description:
A constraint is an expression which has to stay true while a simulation runs, for example that a concentration stays inside the range in which a rate law was measured. It does not change anything in the model: as soon as it is violated, the results from that moment on are no longer valid, and the software has to tell the user.

The report shows the rendered condition and the message which explains a violation.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on a <constraint> is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to a mathematical expression (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000064, "mathematical expression").
The order of subelements within <constraint> must be the following: <math>, <message>. The <message> element is optional, but if present, must follow the <math> element.
A <constraint> object may have the optional attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a Constraint object.

types/Constraint/math.label: math
types/Constraint/math.summary: the condition which has to stay true
types/Constraint/math.description:
The math is an expression which returns a boolean value. It is checked at the start of the simulation and at every moment after it.

The report renders the condition in the column "math" and in the inspector.
types/Constraint/math.default: the constraint puts no restriction on the model

rules.message: A <constraint>'s <math> expression must evaluate to a value of type Boolean.
A <constraint> object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/Constraint/message.label: message
types/Constraint/message.summary: the text which is shown when the condition is violated
types/Constraint/message.description:
The message is XHTML written for the user of a simulation, for example "the concentration of S1 left the range of the rate law". It is the place where the model author explains why the constraint exists.

The report shows the message next to the condition.
types/Constraint/message.default: nothing is shown to the user when the condition is violated

rules.message: The contents of the <message> element in a <constraint> must be explicitly placed in the XHTML XML namespace.
The contents of the <message> element must not contain an XML declaration (i.e., a string of the form "<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>" or similar).
The contents of the <message> element must not contain an XML DOCTYPE declaration (i.e., a string beginning with the characters "<!DOCTYPE".

The XHTML content inside a <constraint>'s <message> element can only take one of the following general forms: (1) a complete XHTML document beginning with the element <html> and ending with </html>; (2) the "body" portion of a document beginning with the element <body> and ending with </body>; or (3) XHTML content that is permitted within a <body> ... </body> elements.
A <constraint> object may contain at most one <message> subobject.

types/DefaultTerm.label: DefaultTerm
types/DefaultTerm.summary: the level of a transition in every state no function term covers
types/DefaultTerm.description:
The default term carries no condition: it is what makes the transition table of a [transition](glossary:types/Transition) total, the row "otherwise" behind the [function terms](glossary:types/FunctionTerm). Every transition has exactly one of them.

The specification notes that the class is not derived from `SBase` while libsbml gives it the full surface of one, so the report reads it as it reads every other element, with its meta id, its SBO term, its notes and its annotations.

rules.message: A <defaultTerm> object may have the optional 'metaid' and 'sboTerm' defined by SBML Level 3 Core. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace or the Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on a <defaultTerm> object.
A <defaultTerm> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on a <defaultTerm>.
A <defaultTerm> object must have the required attributes 'qual:resultLevel'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on a <defaultTerm> object.

types/DefaultTerm/resultLevel.label: resultLevel
types/DefaultTerm/resultLevel.summary: the level the outputs take where no function term holds
types/DefaultTerm/resultLevel.description:
The result level is a whole number which cannot be negative, and it is required. In most files it is zero, which reads as "the entity is off unless one of the terms switches it on".

The report shows it as the last row of the table of the terms in the inspector of the transition, under the condition "otherwise".

rules.message: The attribute 'qual:resultLevel' in <defaultTerm> must be of the data type 'integer'.
The attribute 'qual:resultLevel' in <defaultTerm> must not be negative.

types/Delay.label: Delay
types/Delay.summary: the formula which gives the time between the trigger of an event and its execution
types/Delay.description:
The delay of an [event](glossary:types/Event) postpones its assignments: the event fires at one moment and is carried out later. It is an element of its own, which a model can annotate and explain; whether the values of the assignments are taken from the moment of the trigger or from the moment of the execution is decided by the flag "values from trigger time" of the event.

The report shows the delay as an element of its own and its rendered formula in the table and in the inspector of the event.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on a <delay> is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to a mathematical expression (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000064, "mathematical expression").
A Delay object may have the optional attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a Delay object.

types/Delay/math.label: math
types/Delay/math.summary: the formula which gives the time between the trigger and the execution
types/Delay/math.description:
The math is evaluated at the moment the event triggers and has to give a value which is not negative, in the time units of the model. An event without a delay is executed immediately.

The report renders the formula in the column "delay" of the events and in the inspector, and links the elements it reads.
types/Delay/math.default: the event is executed as one without a delay

rules.message: A Delay object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/Deletion.label: Deletion
types/Deletion.summary: an element which is removed from a submodel before it is instantiated
types/Deletion.description:
A deletion names one element of the model a [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) instantiates and removes it from the composed model. It is how a model uses a part of another model: the initial assignment which the containing model provides itself, the reaction which does not belong in the new context, the parameter which is set from outside.

The removal reaches further than the named element. Everything which depends on it goes with it: a species takes the species references which name it, and with them the reactions which become meaningless, and a compartment takes the species inside it.

A deletion carries an identifier of its own, so that a [replaced element](glossary:types/ReplacedElement) can say that it takes the place of what was deleted, and a name, because deletions are shown to modellers.

The report shows the deletions of a submodel in its inspector, links the element every one of them removes and shows each deletion as an element of its own.

rules.message: (Extends validation rule #10301 in the SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core specification.) Within a <model> or <modelDefinition> object, the values of the attributes id and comp:id on every instance of the following classes of objects must be unique across the set of all id and comp:id attribute values of all such objects in a model: the model itself, plus all contained <functionDefinition>, <compartment>, <species>, <reaction>, <speciesReference>, <modifierSpeciesReference>, <event>, and <parameter> objects, plus the <submodel> and <deletion> objects defined by the Hierarchical Model Composition package, plus any objects defined by any other package with 'package:id' attributes defined as falling in the 'SId' namespace.
Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, an SBaseRef object may only contain a single <sBaseRef> child.

Any one SBML object may only be referenced in one of the following ways: referenced by a single <port> object; referenced by a single <deletion> object; referenced by a single <replacedElement>; be the parent of a single <replacedBy> child; be referenced by one or more <replacedBy> objects; or be referenced by one or more <replacedElement> objects all using the 'deletion' attribute. Essentially, once an object has been referenced in one of these ways it cannot be referenced again.

A <deletion> object must have a value for one, and only one, of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', and 'comp:metaIdRef'. It may also have the optional attributes 'comp:id' and 'comp:name'. No other attributes from the Hierarchical Model Composition namespace are permitted on a <deletion> object.

types/Deletion/idRef.label: idRef
types/Deletion/idRef.summary: the element which is removed, by its identifier
types/Deletion/idRef.description: The identifier is resolved in the model the submodel instantiates, not in the model which declares the deletion.

rules.message: The value of a 'comp:idRef' attribute on an <sBaseRef> object must be the identifier of an object contained in (that is, within the SId namespace of) the <model> referenced by that <sBaseRef>. This includes objects with 'id' attributes defined in packages other than SBML Level 3 Core or the Hierarchical Model Composition package.
The value of a 'comp:idRef' attribute on an SBaseRef object must always conform to the syntax of the SBML data type SId.
A <deletion> object must point to another object; that is, a <deletion> object must always have a value for one of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', or 'comp:metaIdRef'

A <deletion> object can only point to one other object; that is, a given <deletion> object can only have a value for one of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', or 'comp:metaIdRef'

types/Deletion/metaIdRef.label: metaIdRef
types/Deletion/metaIdRef.summary: the element which is removed, by its meta id
types/Deletion/metaIdRef.description: This is the way to delete an element which carries no identifier, for example a rule or a reaction written without one.

rules.message: The value of a 'comp:metaIdRef' attribute on an <sBaseRef> object must be the value of a 'comp:metaid' attribute on an element contained in the <model> referenced by that <sBaseRef>.
The value of a 'comp:metaIdRef' attribute on an SBaseRef object must always conform to the syntax of the XML data type ID.
A <deletion> object must point to another object; that is, a <deletion> object must always have a value for one of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', or 'comp:metaIdRef'

A <deletion> object can only point to one other object; that is, a given <deletion> object can only have a value for one of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', or 'comp:metaIdRef'

types/Deletion/portRef.label: portRef
types/Deletion/portRef.summary: the port of the submodel whose element is removed
types/Deletion/portRef.description: The deletion names a [port](glossary:types/Port) of the model the submodel instantiates, and the element behind that port is what is removed. Naming the port instead of the element is the friendlier way, because the port is the interface the other model offers.

rules.message: The value of a 'comp:portRef' attribute on an <sBaseRef> object must be the identifier of a <port> object in the <model> referenced by that <sBaseRef>.
The value of a 'comp:portRef' attribute on an SBaseRef object must always conform to the syntax of the SBML data type SId.
A <deletion> object must point to another object; that is, a <deletion> object must always have a value for one of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', or 'comp:metaIdRef'

A <deletion> object can only point to one other object; that is, a given <deletion> object can only have a value for one of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', or 'comp:metaIdRef'

types/Deletion/sbaseRef.label: sBaseRef
types/Deletion/sbaseRef.summary: the reference which reaches into a submodel of the submodel
types/Deletion/sbaseRef.description: A deletion which names a submodel of the instantiated model carries a [nested reference](glossary:types/SBaseRef) which names the element inside it, so that an element of a sub-submodel can be removed.

rules.message: If an <sBaseRef> object contains an <sBaseRef> child, the parent <sBaseRef> must point to a <submodel> object, or a <port> that itself points to a <submodel> object.
Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, an SBaseRef object may only contain a single <sBaseRef> child.
The 'sbaseRef' spelling of an SBaseRef child of an SBaseRef object is considered deprecated, and 'sBaseRef' should be used instead.

types/Deletion/unitRef.label: unitRef
types/Deletion/unitRef.summary: the unit definition which is removed
types/Deletion/unitRef.description: Unit identifiers live in a namespace of their own. The units which SBML reserves cannot be deleted.

rules.message: The value of a 'comp:unitRef' attribute on an <sBaseRef> object must be the identifier of a <unitDefinition< object contained in the <model> referenced by that <sBaseRef>.
The value of a 'comp:unitRef' attribute on an SBaseRef object must always conform to the syntax of the SBML data type SId.
A <deletion> object must point to another object; that is, a <deletion> object must always have a value for one of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', or 'comp:metaIdRef'

A <deletion> object can only point to one other object; that is, a given <deletion> object can only have a value for one of the attributes 'comp:portRef', 'comp:idRef', 'comp:unitRef', or 'comp:metaIdRef'

types/Event.label: Event
types/Event.summary: an instantaneous change of the model when a condition becomes true
types/Event.description:
An event describes a discontinuous change: when its trigger turns from false to true, the assignments of the event are executed and set new values for compartments, species, stoichiometries or parameters. A dose which is given at a fixed time, a switch which flips at a threshold or a medium which is exchanged are events. The change can be delayed, and a priority decides which of several simultaneous events is executed first.

The report shows the rendered trigger, the priority and the delay of an event, the flags of its trigger and the table of its assignments, and opens the [trigger](glossary:types/Trigger), the [priority](glossary:types/Priority) and the [delay](glossary:types/Delay) as elements of their own.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on an <event> is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to an occurring entity representation defined in SBO (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000231, "occurring entity representation").
The order of subelements within <event> must be the following: <trigger>, <delay>, <listOfEventAssignments>. The <delay> element is optional, but if present, must follow <trigger>.

An Event object must have the required attribute 'useValuesFromTriggerTime' and in addition may have the optional attributes 'metaid', 'sboTerm', 'id', and 'name'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on an Event object.

types/Event/delay.label: delay
types/Event/delay.summary: the element which postpones the execution of the event
types/Event/delay.description: An event may carry a [delay](glossary:types/Delay), the element whose formula gives the time between the trigger and the execution. An event without a delay is executed immediately.
types/Event/delay.default: the event is executed at the moment it triggers

rules.message: If an <event>'s 'useValuesFromTriggerTime' attribute has the value 'false', then the <event> must contain a <delay> element. The implication of 'useValuesFromTriggerTime=false' is that there is a delay between the time of trigger and the time of value assignments performed by the <event>.
An Event object may contain at most one Delay object.

types/Event/delay.math.label: delay
types/Event/delay.math.summary: the formula which gives the time between the trigger and the execution
types/Event/delay.math.description:
The delay is evaluated at the moment the event triggers and has to be a value which is not negative, in the time units of the model.

The report renders the delay in the column "delay" of the events and in the inspector.
types/Event/delay.math.default: the event is executed as one without a delay

rules.message: A Delay object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/Event/listOfEventAssignments.label: listOfEventAssignments
types/Event/listOfEventAssignments.summary: the changes the event makes when it is executed
types/Event/listOfEventAssignments.description:
The list holds the [event assignments](glossary:types/EventAssignment) of the event, each of which sets one element of the model to the value of a formula.

The report shows the assignments in the column "assignments", every one of them as the element it sets and the formula it assigns, and as a table in the inspector of the event.
types/Event/listOfEventAssignments.default: the event changes nothing when it is executed

rules.message: An <event> object must have at least one <eventAssignment> object in its <listOfEventAssignments>.
An Event object may contain at most one ListOfEventAssignments object.
Apart from the general Notes and Annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML components, a ListOfEventAssignments container object may only contain EventAssignment objects.

types/Event/priority.label: priority
types/Event/priority.summary: the element which orders the event against other events of the same moment
types/Event/priority.description: An event may carry a [priority](glossary:types/Priority), the element whose formula decides which of several events of one moment is executed first. An event without a priority has none, and the order of simultaneous events is then not fixed.
types/Event/priority.default: the order of the event among simultaneous events is not fixed

rules.message: An Event object may contain at most one Priority object.

types/Event/priority.math.label: priority
types/Event/priority.math.summary: the formula which orders this event against other events of the same moment
types/Event/priority.math.description:
When several events are executed at the same moment, the one with the higher priority goes first; a larger number means a higher priority and the value is dimensionless.

The report renders the priority in the column "priority" of the events and in the inspector.
types/Event/priority.math.default: the event behaves as one without a priority

rules.message: An Priority object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/Event/trigger.label: trigger
types/Event/trigger.summary: the condition of the event, as an element of its own
types/Event/trigger.description: Every event has a [trigger](glossary:types/Trigger), the element which holds the condition and the two flags which say how it is read. The report opens it in the inspector, with its own SBO term, notes and annotations.
types/Event/trigger.default: the event can never be triggered

rules.message: An <event> object must have a 'trigger'. In SBML Level 3 Version 2 this rule was relaxed to stating that an <event> object must have at most one 'trigger' element.

types/Event/trigger.initialValue.label: initialValue
types/Event/trigger.initialValue.summary: whether the condition is taken to be true just before the simulation starts
types/Event/trigger.initialValue.description:
To know whether an event may already fire at time zero, a simulator has to know what the condition was just before. With "true" it is taken to have been true, so the event cannot fire at the start; with "false" it may fire immediately.

The report shows the flag as a mark, in the column "initial value" and in the inspector.

rules.message: The attribute 'initialValue' on a Trigger object must have a value of type Boolean.

types/Event/trigger.math.label: trigger
types/Event/trigger.math.summary: the condition whose change from false to true fires the event
types/Event/trigger.math.description:
The trigger holds an expression which returns a boolean value, and the event fires at the moment that expression turns from false to true. It can fire again whenever the expression makes that transition again. An event without a trigger can never fire.

The report renders the condition in the column "trigger" and in the inspector.

rules.message: An <event>'s <trigger> expression must evaluate to a value of type Boolean.
A Trigger object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/Event/trigger.persistent.label: persistent
types/Event/trigger.persistent.summary: whether the event is still executed when its condition becomes false again before execution
types/Event/trigger.persistent.description:
Between the moment an event triggers and the moment it is executed, its condition may turn false again, because the event is delayed or because another event changed the model. With "true" the assignments are carried out anyway, with "false" the event is dropped.

The report shows the flag as a mark, in the column "persistent" and in the inspector.

rules.message: The attribute 'persistent' on a Trigger object must have a value of type Boolean.

types/Event/useValuesFromTriggerTime.label: useValuesFromTriggerTime
types/Event/useValuesFromTriggerTime.summary: whether the assignments use the values of the moment the event was triggered
types/Event/useValuesFromTriggerTime.description:
An event which is delayed is triggered at one moment and executed at another, and the two moments can give different values. With "true" the formulas of the assignments are evaluated when the event triggers, with "false" when it is executed.

The report shows the flag as a mark in the column "values from trigger time".

rules.message: If an <event>'s 'useValuesFromTriggerTime' attribute has the value 'false', then the <event> must contain a <delay> element. The implication of 'useValuesFromTriggerTime=false' is that there is a delay between the time of trigger and the time of value assignments performed by the <event>.

types/EventAssignment.label: EventAssignment
types/EventAssignment.summary: the new value an event gives to one element of the model
types/EventAssignment.description:
An event assignment sets a compartment, a species, a stoichiometry or a parameter to the value of its formula at the moment the event is executed. The element must not be constant, because a constant cannot be changed by an event.

The report shows an event assignment as an element of its own, with a link to the element it changes and the rendered formula.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on an <eventAssignment> is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to a mathematical expression (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000064, "mathematical expression").

An EventAssignment object must have the required attribute 'variable' and may have the optional attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on an EventAssignment object.

types/EventAssignment/math.label: math
types/EventAssignment/math.summary: the formula which computes the new value
types/EventAssignment/math.description:
The math is an arbitrary expression over the elements of the model. Whether it is evaluated when the event triggers or when it is executed is decided by the flag "values from trigger time" of the event.

The report renders the formula in the table of the event and in the inspector.
types/EventAssignment/math.default: nothing is assigned when the event is executed

rules.message: An EventAssignment object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/EventAssignment/variable.label: variable
types/EventAssignment/variable.description:
The variable names the compartment, species, species reference or parameter which receives the new value. It must not be constant.

The report links the named element in the table of the event and in the inspector.

rules.message: In each <event>, the value of the 'variable' field within every <eventAssignment> definition must be unique across the set of all <eventAssignment>s within that <event>.
An identifier used as the value of 'variable' in an <eventAssignment> cannot also appear as the value of 'variable' in an <assignmentRule>.

The value of the attribute 'variable' in an <eventAssignment> can only be the identifier of a <compartment>, <species>, model-wide <parameter> definition, or (in Level 3) <speciesReference>, or (in Level 3 Version 2), any identifier in the SId namespace of the model belonging to an element defined by an SBML Level 3 package as having with mathematical meaning.

Any <compartment>, <species>, <parameter>, or (in Level 3) <speciesReference> definition whose identifier is used as the value of 'variable' in an <eventAssignment> must have a value of 'false' for its 'constant' attribute.

types/ExternalModelDefinition.label: ExternalModelDefinition
types/ExternalModelDefinition.summary: a model of another SBML file which this document can instantiate
types/ExternalModelDefinition.description:
An external model definition makes a model of another file available under an identifier of this document, so that a [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) can instantiate it. It is a declaration, not a use: it says where the file is and which model inside it is meant. The identifier belongs to this document and is not the identifier of the model it points at.

The report shows the external model definitions of a document next to its models, and it follows one to the model it names where it was given the document at its source: another entry of the same COMBINE archive, or a file next to a model which was read from a directory, as the examples are. The references of the [submodels](glossary:types/Submodel) which instantiate it, the [replacements](glossary:types/ReplacedElement), the [deletions](glossary:types/Deletion) and the [ports](glossary:types/Port), then end at the element they name inside that model. The report never fetches a document, and the [status](glossary:types/ExternalModelDefinition) of the definition says how far it could be followed.

rules.message: The values of the attributes 'id' and 'comp:id' on every instance of all <model>, <modelDefinition>, and <externalModelDefinition> objects must be unique across the set of all 'id' and 'comp:id' attribute values of such objects in the SBML document to which they belong.

An <externalModelDefinition> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on an <externalModelDefinition> object.

An <externalModelDefinition> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotation. No other subobjects from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace or the Hierarchical Model Composition namespace are permitted on an <externalModelDefinition> object.

An <externalModelDefinition> object must have the attributes 'comp:id' and 'comp:source', and may have the optional attributes 'comp:name', 'comp:modelRef', and 'comp:md5'. No other attributes from the Hierarchical Model Composition namespace are permitted on an <externalModelDefinition> object.

types/ExternalModelDefinition/md5.label: md5
types/ExternalModelDefinition/md5.summary: the checksum of the document at the source
types/ExternalModelDefinition/md5.description:
The checksum is optional and is the md5 sum of the whole file at the source, as it was when the model was written. It is how a reader tells whether the file they reach is the file the composed model was built against, which matters when the source is a URL that somebody else maintains.

The report shows the checksum in the inspector of the external model definition and compares it with the document it has at the source. It does not fetch a file, so the checksum of a remote source is not checked.
types/ExternalModelDefinition/md5.default: nothing checks that the document at the source is the one the definition was written against

rules.message: The value of the 'comp:md5' attribute, if present on an <externalModelDefinition> object, should match the calculated MD5 checksum of the SBML document referenced by the 'comp:source' attribute.
The value of a comp:md5 attribute on an <externalModelDefinition> object must always conform to the syntax of type string.

types/ExternalModelDefinition/modelRef.label: modelRef
types/ExternalModelDefinition/modelRef.summary: the identifier of the model inside the referenced file
types/ExternalModelDefinition/modelRef.description:
The reference names a model or another external model definition of the document at the source. When it is not set, the main model of that file is meant, which is the case a model without an identifier leaves. Following a chain of external model definitions has to end at a model.

The report shows the reference in the inspector and follows it where it has the document at the source, through a chain of external model definitions to the model at its end.
types/ExternalModelDefinition/modelRef.default: the main model of the document at the source

rules.message: The value of the 'comp:modelRef' attribute on an <externalModelDefinition> object must be the value of an id attribute on a <model>, <modelDefinition>, or <externalModelDefinition> object in the SBML document referenced by the 'comp:source' attribute.
The value of a comp:modelRef attribute on an <externalModelDefinition> object must always conform to the syntax of the SBML data type SId.

An <externalModelDefinition> object must not reference an <externalModelDefinition> in a different SBML document that, in turn, refers back to the original <externalModelDefinition object, whether directly or indirectly through a chain of <externalModelDefinition> objects.

types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.label: document
types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.summary: the entry of the archive which the source names
types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.description:
The location of the entry in the [manifest](glossary:concepts/manifest) of the COMBINE archive, as soon as there is an entry at the source, whether or not the model could be found in it. For a chain of external model definitions it is the entry of the last document which was found.

The inspector links the entry when the report has a model of it.

types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.label: md5 check
types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.summary: whether the document at the source has the checksum the definition states
types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.description:
The report computes the md5 sum of the document it has at the source and compares it with the md5 of the definition. It is not set when the definition states no checksum or when the report has no document to compare with.

A checksum which does not match says that the file is not the one the composed model was written against. The report states the mismatch and still follows the definition, because the document in the archive is the one the model will be run with.

types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.label: model
types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.summary: the model the external model definition names
types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.description:
The [model](glossary:types/Model) or model definition of the other document which the model reference names, the main model of that document where no model reference is set, and the model at the end of the chain where the reference names another external model definition.

The inspector links the model, which opens the report of the other entry, and the link is shown under "References" of the definition and under "Referenced by" of the model.

types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.label: status
types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.summary: how far the report could follow the external model definition
types/ExternalModelDefinition/resolution.description:
The report reads the documents it was given and never fetches one, so whether it can follow an external model definition depends on where its source points. The status is one of six:

- `resolved`: the document at the source is part of the report and holds the model. The references into the [submodels](glossary:types/Submodel) of this definition end at the element they name.
- `remoteSource`: the source is a URI with a scheme, such as a URL. The report does not fetch it, so that the time of a report does not depend on another server and a model cannot make the server request an address.
- `notFound`: the source is a relative location and the report has no document there. This is the status of every external model definition of an SBML file which is uploaded on its own; a COMBINE archive which holds both files resolves it.
- `notSbml`: there is a file at the source, but it holds no SBML model the report could read.
- `modelNotFound`: the document at the source has no model with the identifier the model reference names, or no model at all.
- `circular`: the model reference names an external model definition of the other document, and following the chain comes back to where it started.

Unless the status is `resolved`, the references into the submodels end at the submodel.

types/ExternalModelDefinition/source.label: source
types/ExternalModelDefinition/source.summary: the location of the SBML file which holds the model
types/ExternalModelDefinition/source.description:
The source is a URI, which may be a URL, a URN or a location relative to this document. The whole file at that location is referenced and it has to be an SBML Level 3 Version 1 document; earlier levels and versions are not supported by the package.

The report shows the source in the inspector of the external model definition. A relative source is resolved against the location of the document which names it, inside the COMBINE archive both are entries of. A source with a scheme, such as a URL, is shown and never fetched.

rules.message: The value of the 'comp:source' attribute on an <externalModelDefinition> object must reference an SBML Level 3 document.
The value of a 'comp:source' attribute on an <externalModelDefinition> object must always conform to the syntax of the XML Schema 1.0 data type 'anyURI'.

types/FluxBound.label: FluxBound
types/FluxBound.summary: a constraint on the flux of a reaction, as fbc Version 1 writes it
types/FluxBound.description:
A flux bound of the first version of the package is an object of the model which names a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction), an operation and a value, so that two of them are needed to keep a flux inside an interval and one with the operation `equal` fixes it.

Version 2 removed the construct: a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) names the [parameters](glossary:types/Parameter) of its lower and its upper bound instead, which lets other elements of the model compute a bound and keeps one bound in one place for many reactions. The report shows a flux bound only for a document which is written in Version 1, where it is the only place the capacity of a reaction is stated.

rules.message: (Extends validation rule #10301 in the SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core specification.) Within a <model> object the values of the attributes id and fbc:id on every instance of the following classes of objects must be unique across the set of all id and fbc:id attribute values of all such objects in a model: the model itself, plus all contained <functionDefinition>, <compartment>, <species>, <reaction>, <speciesReference>, <modifierSpeciesReference>, <event>, and <parameter> objects, plus the <fluxBound>, <objective>, <fluxObjective>, <geneProduct> and <geneProductAssociation> objects defined by the Flux Balance Constraints package.
A <fluxBound> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <fluxBound>.
A <fluxBound> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <fluxBound>.

A <fluxBound> object must have the required attributes 'fbc:reaction', 'fbc:operation' and 'fbc:value', and may have the optional attributes 'fbc:id' and 'fbc:name'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespace are permitted on a <fluxBound> object.

types/FluxBound/operation.label: operation
types/FluxBound/operation.summary: how the flux is related to the value: greaterEqual, lessEqual or equal
types/FluxBound/operation.description:
The operation says which side of the value the flux has to stay on. `greaterEqual` and `lessEqual` are the lower and the upper bound, `equal` fixes the flux at the value, which is how a measured exchange rate is written.

The report shows the operation next to the value.

rules.message: The attribute 'fbc:operation' of a <fluxBound> must be of the data type FbcOperation and thus it's value must be one of 'lessEqual', 'greaterEqual' or 'equal'.

The combined set of all <fluxBound>'s with identical values for 'fbc:reaction' must be consistent. That is while it is possible to define a lower and an upper bound for a reaction, it is not possible to define multiple lower or upper bounds.

types/FluxBound/reaction.label: reaction
types/FluxBound/reaction.summary: the reaction whose flux the bound constrains
types/FluxBound/reaction.description: The attribute is required and names a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) of the model. The report links it, and the inspector of the reaction lists every bound which constrains it under "referenced by", which is where the capacity of a reaction of a Version 1 model is read.

rules.message: The attribute 'fbc:reaction' of a <fluxBound> must be of the data type SIdRef.
The value of the attribute 'fbc:reaction' of a <fluxBound> object must be the identifier of an existing <reaction> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

The combined set of all <fluxBound>'s with identical values for 'fbc:reaction' must be consistent. That is while it is possible to define a lower and an upper bound for a reaction, it is not possible to define multiple lower or upper bounds.

types/FluxBound/value.label: value
types/FluxBound/value.summary: the number the flux is compared with
types/FluxBound/value.description: The value carries the units of a reaction flux, extent per time, which the model defines globally. An infinite value states that the flux is not bounded in that direction, and the report shows it as the [sign of infinity](glossary:concepts/number) with the direction of that bound.

rules.message: The attribute 'fbc:value' of a <fluxBound> must be of the data type double.

types/FluxObjective.label: FluxObjective
types/FluxObjective.summary: one term of an objective: a reaction weighted by a coefficient
types/FluxObjective.description:
A flux objective names the [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) whose flux enters the objective function and the number the flux is multiplied with. An [objective](glossary:types/Objective) is the sum of its flux objectives, so a genome scale model usually carries one term of coefficient one on its biomass reaction.

It is an element of the report and not a row of its objective, because the specification derives it from `SBase`: it may carry an identifier, a name, an SBO term, notes and annotations, and the reference to its reaction starts here, not at the objective around it.

rules.message: (Extends validation rule #10301 in the SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core specification.) Within a <model> object the values of the attributes id and fbc:id on every instance of the following classes of objects must be unique across the set of all id and fbc:id attribute values of all such objects in a model: the model itself, plus all contained <functionDefinition>, <compartment>, <species>, <reaction>, <speciesReference>, <modifierSpeciesReference>, <event>, and <parameter> objects, plus the <fluxBound>, <objective>, <fluxObjective>, <geneProduct> and <geneProductAssociation> objects defined by the Flux Balance Constraints package.
A <fluxObjective> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <fluxObjective>.
A <fluxObjective> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <fluxObjective>.

A <fluxObjective> object must have the required attributes 'fbc:reaction' and 'fbc:coefficient', and may have the optional attributes 'fbc:id' and 'fbc:name'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespace are permitted on a <fluxObjective> object.

types/FluxObjective/coefficient.label: coefficient
types/FluxObjective/coefficient.summary: the number the flux of the reaction is multiplied with
types/FluxObjective/coefficient.description:
The coefficient is a signed number and carries no units, since the term takes the units of the flux, extent per time. A negative coefficient turns a term of a maximisation into one which is pushed down, which is how one objective can trade growth against the uptake of a substrate.

In a strict model the coefficient has to be a finite number. The report shows it next to the reaction.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:coefficient' of a <fluxObjective> object must conform to the syntax of the SBML data type 'double'.
When the value of the <model> 'fbc:strict' attribute is true, the value of the attribute 'fbc:coefficient' of a <fluxObjective> object must not be set to 'NaN', 'INF' or '-INF'.

types/FluxObjective/reaction.label: reaction
types/FluxObjective/reaction.summary: the reaction whose flux this term of the objective weighs
types/FluxObjective/reaction.description: The attribute is required and names a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) of the model. The report links it, and the inspector of that reaction shows the flux objective under "referenced by", which is how the reactions an analysis optimises are found.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:reaction' of a <fluxObjective> object must conform to the syntax of the SBML data type 'SIdRef'.
The value of the attribute 'fbc:reaction' of a <fluxObjective> object must be the identifier of an existing <reaction> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/FluxObjective/reaction2.label: reaction2
types/FluxObjective/reaction2.summary: the second reaction of a mixed quadratic term, from Version 3 on
types/FluxObjective/reaction2.description:
A quadratic flux objective which names a second [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) weighs the product of the two fluxes, `coefficient * J1 * J2`, instead of the square of one. The attribute exists from Version 3 of the package on and is empty in every earlier document.

The report links the reaction next to the first one.
types/FluxObjective/reaction2.default: a quadratic term is the square of the flux of the first reaction

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:reaction2' of a <fluxObjective> object must conform to the syntax of the SBML data type 'SIdRef'.
The value of the attribute 'fbc:reaction2' of a <fluxObjective> object must be the identifier of an existing <reaction> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/FluxObjective/variableType.label: variableType
types/FluxObjective/variableType.summary: whether the flux enters the objective linearly or quadratically
types/FluxObjective/variableType.description:
The type is `linear`, the classical case in which the flux appears as it is, or `quadratic`, in which it appears squared or multiplied by the flux of the second reaction. Without it a quadratic term reads like a linear one, and `Minimize: 1 R1 + [4 R2^2]/2` and `Minimize: 1 R1 + 4 R2` cannot be told apart.

The attribute is required from Version 3 of the package on and does not exist before it, so a Version 1 or Version 2 document leaves it empty and every term of its objectives is linear.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:variableType' of a <fluxObjective> object must conform to the syntax of SBML data type 'FbcVariableType' and may only take on the allowed values of 'FbcVariableType' defined in SBML; that is, the value must be one of the following: 'linear' or 'quadratic'.

types/FunctionDefinition.label: FunctionDefinition
types/FunctionDefinition.summary: a named function which the mathematics of the model can call
types/FunctionDefinition.description:
A function definition gives a name to a formula with arguments, so that a rate law which appears in many reactions is written once. The capabilities are deliberately limited: a function may only use its own arguments and other functions, it cannot read a species or a parameter, and it cannot call itself.

The report shows the body of the function as rendered mathematics, in the table and in the inspector.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on a <functionDefinition> is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to a mathematical expression (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000064, "mathematical expression").

FunctionDefinition object must have the required attribute 'id', and may have the optional attributes 'metaid', 'sboTerm' and 'name'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a FunctionDefinition object.

types/FunctionDefinition/math.label: math
types/FunctionDefinition/math.summary: the formula of the function, with its arguments
types/FunctionDefinition/math.description:
The math of a function definition is a MathML lambda expression: it declares the arguments and the expression which is computed from them. It is the only place in SBML core where a lambda is allowed.

The report renders the formula and shows it in the column "math" and in the inspector.
types/FunctionDefinition/math.default: the function has no mathematical meaning in SBML core

rules.message: The top-level element within <math> in a <functionDefinition> is restricted.
Inside the <lambda> of a <functionDefinition>, the identifier of that <functionDefinition> cannot appear as the value of a <ci> element. SBML functions are not permitted to be recursive.

Inside the <lambda> of a <functionDefinition>, if a <ci> element is not the first element within a MathML <apply>, then the <ci>'s value can only be the value of a <bvar> element declared in that <lambda>. In other words, all model entities referenced inside a function definition must be passed arguments to that function.
The value type returned by a <functionDefinition>'s <lambda> must be either Boolean or numeric.
A FunctionDefinition object must contain exactly one MathML math element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/FunctionTerm.label: FunctionTerm
types/FunctionTerm.summary: one row of the transition table: a condition and the level it results in
types/FunctionTerm.description:
A function term is a condition and a level. The condition is ordinary MathML which returns a boolean value and reads the levels of the [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) of the transition; where it holds, the [outputs](glossary:types/Output) take the result level of the term.

The terms of a [transition](glossary:types/Transition) are read in order and the first one which holds decides, so the list of terms with the [default term](glossary:types/DefaultTerm) behind it is the state transition table of the transition.

rules.message: A <functionTerm> object may have the optional 'metaid' and 'sboTerm' defined by SBML Level 3 Core. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace or the Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on a <functionTerm> object.
A <functionTerm> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on a <functionTerm>.
A <functionTerm> object must have the required attributes 'qual:resultLevel'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on a <functionTerm> object.
A <functionTerm> object may contain exactly one MathML <math> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on a <functionTerm> object.

types/FunctionTerm/math.label: math
types/FunctionTerm/math.summary: the condition under which the term decides the level
types/FunctionTerm/math.description:
The math is an expression which returns a boolean value, usually a comparison of the level of a species with the threshold of an input combined with `and`, `or` and `not`. A symbol in it is the identifier of a qualitative species, which means its level, of an [input](glossary:types/Input), which means its threshold level, or of an [output](glossary:types/Output), which means its output level.

The report renders the condition in the table of the terms in the inspector of the transition and links every element the condition reads.

rules.message: The MathML <math> element in a <functionTerm> object should evaluate to a value of type Boolean.

The MathML <math> element in a <functionTerm> object should not use the <csymbol> elements 'time' and 'delay' as these explicitly introduce time into the model. As yet time is not considered within the Qualitative Models package specification.
A <functionTerm> object may contain exactly one MathML <math> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on a <functionTerm> object.

types/FunctionTerm/resultLevel.label: resultLevel
types/FunctionTerm/resultLevel.summary: the level the outputs take where the condition of the term holds
types/FunctionTerm/resultLevel.description:
The result level is a whole number which cannot be negative. An `assignmentLevel` output takes it as its new level, a `production` output gains it multiplied by its output level. The attribute is required.

The report shows it in the column "result level" of the table of the terms in the inspector of the transition.

rules.message: The attribute 'qual:resultLevel' in <functionTerm> must be of the data type 'integer'.
The attribute 'qual:resultLevel' in <functionTerm> must not be negative.

types/GeneProduct.label: GeneProduct
types/GeneProduct.summary: a gene or one of its products which the reactions of the model depend on
types/GeneProduct.description:
A gene product stands for a gene, a transcript or a protein which has to be present for a reaction to run. It exists so that the gene associations of a genome scale reconstruction, which used to be written into the notes of a reaction, have a place of their own and can be referenced.

Because the identifiers of a reconstruction do not follow the rules of an SBML identifier, a gene product carries them in its label, and it is recommended that it also carries an annotation which identifies the gene in a database.

The report shows the gene products of a model in a section of their own, with a link to the associated species, and links them from every reaction which names them.

rules.message: (Extends validation rule #10301 in the SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core specification.) Within a <model> object the values of the attributes id and fbc:id on every instance of the following classes of objects must be unique across the set of all id and fbc:id attribute values of all such objects in a model: the model itself, plus all contained <functionDefinition>, <compartment>, <species>, <reaction>, <speciesReference>, <modifierSpeciesReference>, <event>, and <parameter> objects, plus the <fluxBound>, <objective>, <fluxObjective>, <geneProduct> and <geneProductAssociation> objects defined by the Flux Balance Constraints package.
A <GeneProduct> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <GeneProduct>.
A <GeneProduct> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <GeneProduct>.

A <GeneProduct> object must have the required attributes 'fbc:id' and 'fbc:label' may have the optional attributes 'fbc:name' and 'fbc:associatedSpecies'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespace are permitted on a <GeneProduct> object.

types/GeneProduct/associatedSpecies.label: associatedSpecies
types/GeneProduct/associatedSpecies.summary: the species of the model which stands for this gene product
types/GeneProduct/associatedSpecies.description:
Some reconstructions model a gene product as a [species](glossary:types/Species) which participates in reactions. The attribute connects the two, and when it is set it names an existing species of the model.

The report links the species in the column "associated species" and in the inspector.

rules.message: The attribute 'fbc:associatedSpecies' on a <GeneProduct> must be the identifier of an existing <Species> defined in the enclosing <Model>.

types/GeneProduct/label.label: label
types/GeneProduct/label.summary: the identifier under which the source of the model knows the gene
types/GeneProduct/label.description:
The label carries the gene identifier as it is written in the reconstruction, for example `b3670` or `Rv0649`. It is required, because the identifier of the gene product itself has to follow the rules of an SBML identifier and the gene identifier usually does not.

The report shows the label in the column "label" and in the inspector.

rules.message: The attribute 'fbc:label' on a <GeneProduct> must be of the data type 'string'.
The attribute 'fbc:label' on a <GeneProduct> must be unique among the set of all <GeneProduct> elements defined in the <Model>.

types/GeneProductAssociation.label: GeneProductAssociation
types/GeneProductAssociation.summary: the genes a reaction needs, as the tree of operators over them
types/GeneProductAssociation.description:
A gene product association is what a genome scale reconstruction knows about the genetics of a reaction: which genes have to be expressed for the reaction to carry a flux. It belongs to one [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) and holds exactly one node, which is an [and](glossary:types/And), an [or](glossary:types/Or) or a single [gene product reference](glossary:types/GeneProductRef).

The tree is the meaning of the construct, not a decoration of it. A knockout analysis removes a gene, evaluates the tree of every reaction and switches off the reactions whose tree becomes false, so an `and` and an `or` of the same genes describe two different organisms.

The report shows the association in the inspector of its reaction and gives every node of the tree a page of its own, so that a reader can follow a gene into the reactions which depend on it.

rules.message: (Extends validation rule #10301 in the SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core specification.) Within a <model> object the values of the attributes id and fbc:id on every instance of the following classes of objects must be unique across the set of all id and fbc:id attribute values of all such objects in a model: the model itself, plus all contained <functionDefinition>, <compartment>, <species>, <reaction>, <speciesReference>, <modifierSpeciesReference>, <event>, and <parameter> objects, plus the <fluxBound>, <objective>, <fluxObjective>, <geneProduct> and <geneProductAssociation> objects defined by the Flux Balance Constraints package.

A <GeneProductAssociation> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <GeneProductAssociation.

A <GeneProductAssociation> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <GeneProductAssociation.

A <GeneProductAssociation> object may have the optional attributes 'fbc:id' and 'fbc:name'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespace are permitted on a <GeneProductAssociation> object.
A <GeneProductAssociation> object must have one and only one of the concrete <Association> objects: <GeneProductRef>, <And> or <Or>.

types/GeneProductAssociation/association.label: association
types/GeneProductAssociation/association.summary: the single node the association holds
types/GeneProductAssociation/association.description:
The node is an [and](glossary:types/And), an [or](glossary:types/Or) or a [gene product reference](glossary:types/GeneProductRef); the last of them is the whole association of a reaction which depends on one gene alone.

The report renders the node and everything below it as the expression it stands for.

rules.message: A <GeneProductAssociation> object must have one and only one of the concrete <Association> objects: <GeneProductRef>, <And> or <Or>.

types/GeneProductRef.label: GeneProductRef
types/GeneProductRef.summary: the leaf of an association: one gene product the reaction depends on
types/GeneProductRef.description:
A gene product reference is where an association names a gene. It carries the identifier of a [gene product](glossary:types/GeneProduct) of the model and nothing else, so it is the place at which the tree of a reaction meets the list of the genes.

The report makes it an element of its own because the reference is where the file writes the identifier: the link to the gene product starts here, and the same gene may be named by several references of one reaction.

rules.message: A <GeneProductRef> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <GeneProductRef>.
A <GeneProductRef> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a <GeneProductRef>.

A <GeneProductRef> object must have the required attribute 'fbc:geneProduct' and may have the optional attribute 'fbc:id'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespace are permitted on a <> object.

types/GeneProductRef/geneProduct.label: geneProduct
types/GeneProductRef/geneProduct.summary: the gene product this leaf of the association names
types/GeneProductRef/geneProduct.description: The attribute is required and names a [gene product](glossary:types/GeneProduct) of the same model. The report shows the identifier the reference writes and links the gene product behind it.

rules.message: The attribute 'fbc:geneProduct' on a <GeneProductRef> must be of the data type 'SIdRef'.
The attribute 'fbc:geneProduct' on a <GeneProductRef> if set, must refer to 'id' of a <GeneProduct> in the <Model>.

types/InitialAssignment.label: InitialAssignment
types/InitialAssignment.summary: a formula which computes the value of an element at the start of the simulation
types/InitialAssignment.description:
An initial assignment computes the value of a compartment, a species, a parameter or a stoichiometry before the simulation starts, from the values of other elements. It exists because the attributes of an element can only hold a literal number, and an initial value is often derived from other quantities. It applies up to the start of time and, unlike an assignment rule, it may also set a constant.

The report shows the element which is assigned, the rendered formula and the units the formula produces.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on an <initialAssignment> is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to a mathematical expression (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000064, "mathematical expression").

An InitialAssignment object must have the required attribute 'symbol' and may have the optional attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on an InitialAssignment object.

There must not be circular dependencies in the combined set of <initialAssignment>, <assignmentRule> and <kineticLaw> definitions in a model. Each of these constructs has the effect of assigning a value to an identifier (i.e. the identifier given in the field 'symbol' in <initialAssignment>, the field 'variable' in <assignmentRule>, and the field 'id' on the <kineticLaw>'s enclosing <reaction>). Each of these constructs computes the value using a mathematical formula. The formula for a given identifier cannot make reference to a second identifier whose own definition depends directly or indirectly on the first identifier.

types/InitialAssignment/derivedUnits.label: derived units
types/InitialAssignment/derivedUnits.summary: the units of the formula as the report derives them
types/InitialAssignment/derivedUnits.description: The report derives the units of the formula from the units of the quantities it uses and renders them as a formula. Comparing them with the units of the assigned element is the quickest check of an initial assignment.

types/InitialAssignment/math.label: math
types/InitialAssignment/math.summary: the formula which computes the initial value
types/InitialAssignment/math.description:
The math is an arbitrary expression over the elements of the model. Its units should be the units of the element it assigns to.

The report renders the formula in the column "math" and in the inspector.
types/InitialAssignment/math.default: what is assigned to the symbol stays undefined

rules.message: An InitialAssignment object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/InitialAssignment/symbol.label: symbol
types/InitialAssignment/symbol.summary: the element whose initial value the assignment computes
types/InitialAssignment/symbol.description:
The symbol names the compartment, species, species reference or parameter which receives the value. It is called symbol rather than variable because an initial assignment may also set an element which is constant.

The report links the named element in the column "symbol" and in the inspector.

rules.message: The value of 'symbol' in an <initialAssignment> definition must be the identifier of an existing <compartment>, <species>, or <parameter> defined in the model or <speciesReference> in Level 3, or in Level 3 Version 2, any identifier in the SId namespace of the model belonging to an element defined by an SBML Level 3 package as having with mathematical meaning.
A given identifier cannot appear as the value of more than one 'symbol' field across the set of <initialAssignment>s in a model.
The value of a 'symbol' field in any <initialAssignment> definition cannot also appear as the value of a 'variable' field in an <assignmentRule>.
The identifier given as the value of a 'symbol' attribute in any <initialAssignment> definition cannot be the identifier of a <compartment> with a 'spatialDimensions' value of 0.

types/Input.label: Input
types/Input.summary: a qualitative species a transition reads, with the sign of its influence
types/Input.description:
An input names the [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) whose level a [transition](glossary:types/Transition) reads. Together with the [outputs](glossary:types/Output) of the transitions the inputs are the influence graph of the model, the picture a reader of a regulatory model actually wants: who acts on whom, and whether the action activates or inhibits.

It is an element of the report and not a row of its transition, because the specification derives it from `SBase`: it may carry an identifier, a name, an SBO term, notes and annotations, and the reference to its species starts here, not at the transition around it.

rules.message: (Extends validation rule #10301 in the SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core specification.) Within a <model> the values of the attributes 'id' and 'qual:id' on every instance of the following classes of objects must be unique across the set of all 'id' and 'qual:id' attribute values of all such objects in a model: the <model> itself, plus all contained <functionDefinition>, <compartment>, <species>, <reaction>, <speciesReference>, <modifierSpeciesReference>, <event>, and <parameter> objects, plus the <qualitativeSpecies>, <transition>, <input> and <output> objects defined by the Qualitative Models package.

An <input> object may have the optional 'metaid' and 'sboTerm' defined by SBML Level 3 Core. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace or the Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on an <input> object.
An <input> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <input>.

An <input> object must have the required attributes 'qual:qualitativeSpecies' as well as 'qual:transitionEffect' and may have the optional attributes 'qual:id', 'qual:name', 'qual:sign' and 'qual:thresholdLevel'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on an <input> object.

types/Input/qualitativeSpecies.label: qualitativeSpecies
types/Input/qualitativeSpecies.summary: the species whose level the transition reads
types/Input/qualitativeSpecies.description: The attribute is required and names a [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) of the model. The report links it, and the inspector of that species shows the input under "referenced by", which is how the transitions that read an entity are found.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'qual:qualitativeSpecies' in an <input> object must be the identifier of an existing <qualitativeSpecies> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/Input/sign.label: sign
types/Input/sign.summary: whether the influence of the species activates or inhibits
types/Input/sign.description:
The sign is `positive` for an activation, `negative` for an inhibition, `dual` where the species does both depending on the level of the others, and `unknown` where the file does not say. The specification adds it for visualisation: the mathematics of the model is in the [function terms](glossary:types/FunctionTerm), and the sign is what lets a reader, or a drawing of the influence graph, see an arrow and a bar without reading the conditions.

The report shows the sign next to the species of the input in the column "inputs" of the transitions and in the table of the inputs in the inspector.
types/Input/sign.default: the model says nothing about the direction of the influence

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'qual:sign' of an <input> object must conform to the syntax of the SBML data type 'sign' and may only take on the allowed values of 'sign' defined in SBML; that is, the value must be one of the following: 'positive', 'negative', 'dual' or 'unknown'.

types/Input/thresholdLevel.label: thresholdLevel
types/Input/thresholdLevel.summary: the level of the species at which the input acts
