The value of a 'comp:extentConversionFactor' attribute on a given <submodel> object must be the identifier of a <parameter> object defined in the same Model containing the <submodel>.

types/Submodel/listOfDeletions.label: listOfDeletions
types/Submodel/listOfDeletions.summary: the elements which are removed from the model before it is instantiated
types/Submodel/listOfDeletions.description:
A deletion names one element of the referenced model which is not wanted in this context. The removal is conceptual: the submodel is everything of the referenced model minus the deleted elements, and minus what depends on them. Every deletion names its element the same four ways a [reference](glossary:types/SBaseRef) of the package does, by port, identifier, unit identifier or meta id.

The report shows the number of deletions in the column "deletions" and the four references of every deletion in the inspector.
types/Submodel/listOfDeletions.default: the referenced model is instantiated whole

rules.message: There may be at most one <listOfDeletions> container object within a <submodel> object.
A <listOfDeletions> container object within a <submodel> object is optional, but if present, must not be empty.
Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfDeletions> container object may only contain <deletion> objects.

types/Submodel/modelRef.label: modelRef
types/Submodel/modelRef.summary: the model which this submodel instantiates
types/Submodel/modelRef.description:
The reference names a [model](glossary:types/Model) definition or an [external model definition](glossary:types/ExternalModelDefinition) of the same document. It is required, a submodel without it has nothing to instantiate.

The report links the model in the column "model" and in the inspector of the submodel.

rules.message: The value of a 'comp:modelRef' attribute on a <submodel> object must always conform to the syntax of the SBML data type SId.
The value of a 'comp:modelRef' attribute on a <submodel> must be the identifier of a <model>, <modelDefinition>, or <externalModelDefinition> object in the same SBML object as the <submodel>.

A <model> or <modelDefinition> object must not contain a <submodel> which references that model object itself. That is, the value of a 'comp:modelRef' attribute on a <submodel> must not be the value of the parent <model> or <modelDefinition>'s 'id' attribute.

A <model> object must not contain a <submodel> which references that <model> indirectly. That is, the 'comp:modelRef' attribute of a <submodel> may not point to the 'id' of a <model> containing a <submodel> object that references the original <model> directly or indirectly through a chain of <model>/<submodel> pairs.

types/Submodel/timeConversionFactor.label: timeConversionFactor
types/Submodel/timeConversionFactor.summary: the parameter which converts the time of the submodel into the time of this model
types/Submodel/timeConversionFactor.description:
The factor is the identifier of a constant, dimensionless [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) of the containing model. One unit of time in the submodel multiplied by the factor is one unit of time here, and every reference to time of the submodel is converted with it: the time and delay symbols, the delays of events, the rate rules and the kinetic laws. The factors of nested submodels multiply.

The report links the parameter in the column "time conversion factor" and in the inspector.
types/Submodel/timeConversionFactor.default: one unit of time in the submodel is one unit of time in this model

rules.message: The value of a 'comp:timeConversionFactor' attribute on a <submodel> object must always conform to the syntax of the SBML data type SId.
The value of a 'comp:timeConversionFactor' attribute on a given <submodel> object must be the identifier of a <parameter> object defined in the same Model containing the <submodel>.

types/Transition.label: Transition
types/Transition.summary: what the level of a qualitative species becomes, and under which condition
types/Transition.description:
A transition is to a qualitative model what a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) with its kinetic law is to a kinetic one: it holds the dynamics. It reads the [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) of its [inputs](glossary:types/Input), it changes those of its [outputs](glossary:types/Output), and its [function terms](glossary:types/FunctionTerm) say which level the outputs take: the result level of the first term whose condition holds, and the level of the [default term](glossary:types/DefaultTerm) where none of them holds.

Its identifier is optional and has no mathematical meaning, because nothing in a qualitative model refers to a transition.

The report shows the transitions of a model in a section of their own, with the species they read and the species they change, and the inspector shows the function terms as the table of condition and result level they are.

rules.message: (Extends validation rule #10301 in the SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core specification.) Within a <model> the values of the attributes 'id' and 'qual:id' on every instance of the following classes of objects must be unique across the set of all 'id' and 'qual:id' attribute values of all such objects in a model: the <model> itself, plus all contained <functionDefinition>, <compartment>, <species>, <reaction>, <speciesReference>, <modifierSpeciesReference>, <event>, and <parameter> objects, plus the <qualitativeSpecies>, <transition>, <input> and <output> objects defined by the Qualitative Models package.

A <transition> object may have the optional 'metaid' and 'sboTerm' defined by SBML Level 3 Core. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace or the Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on a <transition> object.
A <transition> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on a <transition>.
A <transition> object may have the optional attributes 'qual:name' and 'qual:id'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Qualitative Models namespace are permitted on a <transition> object.

A <transition> must have one and only one instance of the <listOfFunctionTerms> objects and may have at most one instance of the <listOfInputs> and <listOfOutputs> objects from the Qualitative Models namespace.

types/Transition/defaultTerm.label: defaultTerm
types/Transition/defaultTerm.summary: the term which holds in every state no function term covers
types/Transition/defaultTerm.description:
Every transition has exactly one [default term](glossary:types/DefaultTerm), which makes the transition table total: whatever the levels of the inputs, some term gives a result level.

The report shows it as the last row of the table of the function terms, under the condition "otherwise".

rules.message: Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfFunctionTerms> container object must contain one and only one <defaultTerm> object and then may only contain <functionTerm> objects.

types/Transition/listOfFunctionTerms.label: listOfFunctionTerms
types/Transition/listOfFunctionTerms.summary: the terms which decide the level, in the order in which they are read
types/Transition/listOfFunctionTerms.description:
The list is the transition table of the transition. Its [terms](glossary:types/FunctionTerm) are read in the order in which the file writes them and the first one whose condition holds decides the result level, so two terms whose conditions overlap are not a contradiction: the earlier one wins.

The report shows the terms as a table of condition and result level in the inspector of the transition, with the default term as its last row.

rules.message: A <transition> must have one and only one instance of the <listOfFunctionTerms> objects and may have at most one instance of the <listOfInputs> and <listOfOutputs> objects from the Qualitative Models namespace.

Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfFunctionTerms> container object must contain one and only one <defaultTerm> object and then may only contain <functionTerm> objects.
No element of the <listOfFunctionTerms> object may cause the level of a <qualitativeSpecies> to exceed the value 'qual:maxLevel' attribute.
No element of the <listOfFunctionTerms> object may cause the level of a <qualitativeSpecies> to become negative.

types/Transition/listOfInputs.label: listOfInputs
types/Transition/listOfInputs.summary: the qualitative species the transition reads
types/Transition/listOfInputs.description:
Every [input](glossary:types/Input) names one [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) whose level the condition of a function term may read, with the threshold at which it matters and the sign of its influence. A transition may list none of them, in which case its terms read no species at all.

The report shows the species of the inputs with their sign in the column "inputs" and the table of the inputs in the inspector.
types/Transition/listOfInputs.default: the function terms of the transition read no species

rules.message: A <transition> must have one and only one instance of the <listOfFunctionTerms> objects and may have at most one instance of the <listOfInputs> and <listOfOutputs> objects from the Qualitative Models namespace.
The <listOfInputs> and <listOfOutputs> subobjects on a <transition> object are optional, but if present, these container object must not be empty.
Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfInputs> container object may only contain <input> objects.

types/Transition/listOfOutputs.label: listOfOutputs
types/Transition/listOfOutputs.summary: the qualitative species the transition changes
types/Transition/listOfOutputs.description:
Every [output](glossary:types/Output) names one [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) whose level the transition sets or increases. A transition without outputs changes nothing, which is why a model which does something has at least one.

The report shows the species of the outputs in the column "outputs" and the table of the outputs in the inspector.

rules.message: A <transition> must have one and only one instance of the <listOfFunctionTerms> objects and may have at most one instance of the <listOfInputs> and <listOfOutputs> objects from the Qualitative Models namespace.
The <listOfInputs> and <listOfOutputs> subobjects on a <transition> object are optional, but if present, these container object must not be empty.
Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfOutputs> container object may only contain <output> objects.

types/Trigger.label: Trigger
types/Trigger.summary: the condition of an event, whose change from false to true fires it
types/Trigger.description:
The trigger holds the condition of an [event](glossary:types/Event) as a formula which returns a boolean value, and it decides when the event fires: at the moment the formula turns from false to true. It is an element of its own, so a model can say with an SBO term what kind of condition it is and explain in its notes what the condition stands for.

The report shows the trigger as an element of its own, and its rendered condition and its two flags in the table and in the inspector of the event.

rules.message: The value of the 'sboTerm' attribute on a <trigger> is expected to be an SBO identifier (http://www.biomodels.net/SBO/) referring to a mathematical expression (i.e., terms derived from SBO:0000064, "mathematical expression").

A Trigger object must have the required attributes 'persistent' and 'initialValue', and in addition, may have the optional attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a Trigger object.

types/Trigger/initialValue.label: initialValue
types/Trigger/initialValue.summary: whether the condition is taken to be true just before the simulation starts
types/Trigger/initialValue.description:
To know whether an event may already fire at time zero, a simulator has to know what the condition was just before. With "true" it is taken to have been true, so the event cannot fire at the start; with "false" it may fire immediately.

The report shows the flag as a mark, in the column "initial value" of the events and in the inspector.

rules.message: The attribute 'initialValue' on a Trigger object must have a value of type Boolean.

types/Trigger/math.label: math
types/Trigger/math.summary: the condition whose change from false to true fires the event
types/Trigger/math.description:
The math is an expression which returns a boolean value, and the event fires at the moment it turns from false to true. It can fire again whenever the expression makes that transition again. A trigger without a formula can never fire.

The report renders the condition in the column "trigger" of the events and in the inspector, and links the elements the condition reads.

rules.message: An <event>'s <trigger> expression must evaluate to a value of type Boolean.
A Trigger object must contain exactly one MathML <math> element. The <math> element is optional in L3V2 and beyond.

types/Trigger/persistent.label: persistent
types/Trigger/persistent.summary: whether the event is still executed when its condition becomes false again before execution
types/Trigger/persistent.description:
Between the moment an event triggers and the moment it is executed, its condition may turn false again, because the event is delayed or because another event changed the model. With "true" the assignments are carried out anyway, with "false" the event is dropped.

The report shows the flag as a mark, in the column "persistent" of the events and in the inspector.

rules.message: The attribute 'persistent' on a Trigger object must have a value of type Boolean.

types/UncertParameter.label: UncertParameter
types/UncertParameter.summary: one statistical measure of an uncertainty
types/UncertParameter.description:
An uncert parameter is one measure of the [uncertainty](glossary:types/Uncertainty) it belongs to: its mean, its standard deviation, the size of the sample it was measured on, or the distribution the value was drawn from. Its [type](glossary:types/UncertParameter/type) says which of the sixteen measures of the package it is, and the number behind that measure is either its [value](glossary:types/UncertParameter/value) or the element its [var](glossary:types/UncertParameter/var) names.

It is an element of the report and not a row of its uncertainty, because the specification derives it from `SBase` and from the `DistribBase` of the package: it may carry an identifier, a name, an SBO term, notes and annotations, and the notes of a measure are where a file records which paper or which experiment the number comes from, which is what the package exists for.

A measure which is an interval is an [uncert span](glossary:types/UncertSpan), a class of its own, and a measure of the type `distribution` or `externalParameter` carries the parameters which define it as [uncert parameters](glossary:types/UncertParameter/uncertParameters) of its own.

rules.message: An <uncertParameter> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <uncertParameter>.

An <uncertParameter> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <uncertParameter>.

An <uncertParameter> object may have the optional attributes 'distrib:value', 'distrib:var', 'distrib:units', 'distrib:type' and 'distrib:definitionURL'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Distributions namespaces are permitted on an <uncertParameter> object.

An <uncertParameter> object may contain one and only one instance of the <listOfUncertParameters> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Distributions namespaces are permitted on an <uncertParameter> object.

types/UncertParameter/definitionUrl.label: definitionURL
types/UncertParameter/definitionUrl.summary: what a distribution or an external parameter means
types/UncertParameter/definitionUrl.description:
A parameter of the type `distribution` may name the distribution it stands for, and a parameter of the type `externalParameter` has to name what it is: an entry of an ontology such as ProbOnto, the `csymbol` of a distribution of this package, or another definition which says what the number means. No other type of parameter carries it, because the specification defines the others completely.

The report shows the last segment of the url as a link in the table of the parameters of an uncertainty.
types/UncertParameter/definitionUrl.default: the type of the measure says completely what it means

rules.message: The attribute 'distrib:definitionURL' on an <uncertParameter> must have a value of data type 'string'.

types/UncertParameter/math.label: math
types/UncertParameter/math.summary: the formula which defines a distribution
types/UncertParameter/math.description:
Only a parameter of the type `distribution` or `externalParameter` carries math, and for a distribution the formula is the distribution itself, usually one of the `csymbol` distributions the package defines, such as `normal(2, 2)`.

The report renders the formula and links every element it names, from the parameter which carries the math and not from the uncertainty around it, so that two parameters of one uncertainty stay apart.
types/UncertParameter/math.default: a distribution is defined by its definition url and the parameters below it

types/UncertParameter/type.label: type
types/UncertParameter/type.summary: which statistical measure the parameter is
types/UncertParameter/type.description:
The attribute is required and is one of sixteen values. Ten of them are a single number: `mean`, `median`, `mode`, `variance`, `standardDeviation`, `standardError`, `coefficientOfVariation`, `skewness`, `kurtosis` and `sampleSize`. Four of them are an interval and are written as an [uncert span](glossary:types/UncertSpan): `range`, `confidenceInterval`, `credibleInterval` and `interquartileRange`, where the confidence and the credible interval are always the 95 percent interval. The last two say where a value comes from: `distribution`, the distribution it was drawn from, and `externalParameter`, a measure this specification does not define, which names what it means in its [definition](glossary:types/UncertParameter/definitionUrl).

The report shows the type in the first column of the parameters of an uncertainty and as the name of a parameter which carries no identifier.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'distrib:type' of an <uncertParameter> object must conform to the syntax of SBML data type 'UncertType' and may only take on the allowed values of 'UncertType' defined in SBML; that is, the value must be one of the following: 'distribution', 'externalParameter', 'coeffientOfVariation', 'kurtosis', 'mean', 'median', 'mode', 'sampleSize', 'skewness', 'standardDeviation', 'standardError', 'variance', 'confidenceInterval', 'credibleInterval', 'interquartileRange' or 'range'.

types/UncertParameter/uncertParameters.label: uncertParameters
types/UncertParameter/uncertParameters.summary: the parameters which define a distribution or an external parameter
types/UncertParameter/uncertParameters.description:
A distribution is defined by the parameters it takes: a Beta distribution by its alpha and its beta, a zeta distribution by its shape. They are uncert parameters of the parameter which names the distribution, of any type and to any depth, and without them a report shows the name of a distribution and none of its numbers.

The report shows every one of them indented below the parameter it defines, in the table of the measures of the uncertainty and in the inspector of that parameter.

rules.message: An <uncertParameter> object may contain one and only one instance of the <listOfUncertParameters> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Distributions namespaces are permitted on an <uncertParameter> object.
Apart from the general notes and annotations subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfUncertParameters> container object may only contain <uncertParameter> objects.

types/UncertParameter/units.label: units
types/UncertParameter/units.summary: the units the measure is given in
types/UncertParameter/units.description:
The units are either a [unit definition](glossary:types/UnitDefinition) of the model or one of the base units of SBML. They are usually the units of the element the uncertainty belongs to, for a mean or a standard deviation, or dimensionless, for a coefficient of variation or a sample size.

The report links the unit definition where the units name one.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'distrib:units' on an <uncertParameter> must have a taken from the following: the identifier of a <unitDefinition> object in the enclosing <model,> or one of the base units in SBML.

types/UncertParameter/value.label: value
types/UncertParameter/value.description:
A measure which is a single number carries it here, in the [units](glossary:types/UncertParameter/units) of the parameter. A file writes either the value or the [var](glossary:types/UncertParameter/var), never both: the value is the measurement as it was made, the var is the element of the model which holds it.

The report shows the value in the column "value" of the parameters of an uncertainty and in the inspector of the parameter.
types/UncertParameter/value.default: a measure which is a single number names the element which holds it in var

rules.message: The attribute 'distrib:value' on an <uncertParameter> must have a value of data type 'double'.

types/UncertParameter/var.label: var
types/UncertParameter/var.summary: the element of the model which holds the number of the measure
types/UncertParameter/var.description:
Where the measure is not a fixed number but a quantity of the model, the parameter names that element instead of writing a value: the standard deviation of a parameter may be a parameter of its own, which a simulation reads and a sampling changes. The identifier of the uncert parameter itself has no mathematical meaning and cannot be used for this, which is why the specification defines the attribute.

The report links the element the var names, and the inspector of that element shows the measure under "referenced by".
types/UncertParameter/var.default: a measure which is a single number writes that number in value

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'distrib:var' of an <uncertParameter> object must be the identifier of an existing object derived from the 'SBase' class and defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/UncertSpan.label: UncertSpan
types/UncertSpan.summary: a measure of an uncertainty which is an interval
types/UncertSpan.description:
Four of the sixteen measures of the package are an interval and not a number: the [range](glossary:types/UncertSpan/type) of a measurement, its 95 percent confidence interval, its 95 percent credible interval and its interquartile range. A span is the [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter) of such a measure, with the two ends of the interval in the place of the single value of a parameter.

Each end is either a number, in [value lower](glossary:types/UncertSpan/valueLower) and [value upper](glossary:types/UncertSpan/valueUpper), or an element of the model, in [var lower](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varLower) and [var upper](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varUpper). An end which is set by neither is not defined, so a span may be open at one end.

The report shows a span as the interval it is, `1 to 4`, with a link where an end names an element.

rules.message: An <uncertSpan> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <uncertSpan>.
An <uncertSpan> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <uncertSpan>.

An <uncertSpan> object may have the optional attributes 'distrib:varLower', 'distrib:valueLower', 'distrib:varUpper' and 'distrib:valueUpper'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Distributions namespaces are permitted on an <uncertSpan> object.

types/UncertSpan/definitionUrl.label: definitionURL
types/UncertSpan/definitionUrl.summary: what an external parameter which is an interval means
types/UncertSpan/definitionUrl.description:
A span of the type `externalParameter` names what its interval is, an entry of an ontology or another definition which says what the two ends mean, the way an [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter/definitionUrl) does. The four intervals the specification defines carry no definition url.

The report shows the last segment of the url as a link in the table of the parameters of an uncertainty.
types/UncertSpan/definitionUrl.default: the four intervals the specification defines say completely what they mean

rules.message: The attribute 'distrib:definitionURL' on an <uncertParameter> must have a value of data type 'string'.

types/UncertSpan/interval.label: interval
types/UncertSpan/interval.summary: the two ends of the span as the interval they stand for
types/UncertSpan/interval.description:
The report shows the four attributes of a span as one row, because they are one interval: `1 to 4` where both ends are numbers, the identifier of the element as a link where an end names one, and `from 1` or `to 4` where the file defines one end only.

The row is the reading of [value lower](glossary:types/UncertSpan/valueLower), [value upper](glossary:types/UncertSpan/valueUpper), [var lower](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varLower) and [var upper](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varUpper), each of which the file writes on its own.

types/UncertSpan/math.label: math
types/UncertSpan/math.summary: the formula of an external parameter which is an interval
types/UncertSpan/math.description:
Only a span of the type `externalParameter` carries math, the way an [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter/math) of the type `distribution` does.

The report renders the formula and links every element it names from the span which carries it.

types/UncertSpan/type.label: type
types/UncertSpan/type.description:
The attribute is required. A span carries one of the four measures which are an interval, `range`, `confidenceInterval`, `credibleInterval` and `interquartileRange`, or `externalParameter`, the measure the package does not define, which may be an interval as well. The other eleven values are a single number and belong to an [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter/type).

The report shows the type in the first column of the parameters of an uncertainty and as the name of a span which carries no identifier.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'distrib:type' of an <uncertParameter> object must conform to the syntax of SBML data type 'UncertType' and may only take on the allowed values of 'UncertType' defined in SBML; that is, the value must be one of the following: 'distribution', 'externalParameter', 'coeffientOfVariation', 'kurtosis', 'mean', 'median', 'mode', 'sampleSize', 'skewness', 'standardDeviation', 'standardError', 'variance', 'confidenceInterval', 'credibleInterval', 'interquartileRange' or 'range'.

types/UncertSpan/uncertParameters.label: uncertParameters
types/UncertSpan/uncertParameters.summary: the parameters which define an external parameter
types/UncertSpan/uncertParameters.description:
A span of the type `externalParameter` may be defined by parameters of its own, the way a [distribution](glossary:types/UncertParameter/uncertParameters) is. The four intervals the specification defines need none, because their two ends define them.

The report shows every one of them indented below the span it defines.

rules.message: An <uncertParameter> object may contain one and only one instance of the <listOfUncertParameters> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Distributions namespaces are permitted on an <uncertParameter> object.
Apart from the general notes and annotations subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfUncertParameters> container object may only contain <uncertParameter> objects.

types/UncertSpan/units.label: units
types/UncertSpan/units.summary: the units both ends of the interval are given in
types/UncertSpan/units.description:
The units of the two ends of the span, which have to be the same, given as a [unit definition](glossary:types/UnitDefinition) of the model or as a base unit of SBML. An end which names an element carries the units of that element instead.

The report links the unit definition where the units name one.
types/UncertSpan/units.default: an end which names an element carries the units of that element

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'distrib:units' on an <uncertParameter> must have a taken from the following: the identifier of a <unitDefinition> object in the enclosing <model,> or one of the base units in SBML.

types/UncertSpan/value.label: value
types/UncertSpan/value.summary: the single number of a measure, which a span does not use
types/UncertSpan/value.description: A span carries its numbers in [value lower](glossary:types/UncertSpan/valueLower) and [value upper](glossary:types/UncertSpan/valueUpper). The attribute belongs to the [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter/value) a span derives from and is left unset by every interval, so the report shows the interval in its place.
types/UncertSpan/value.default: a span carries its numbers in value lower and value upper

rules.message: The attribute 'distrib:value' on an <uncertParameter> must have a value of data type 'double'.

types/UncertSpan/valueLower.label: valueLower
types/UncertSpan/valueLower.summary: the lower end of the interval as a number
types/UncertSpan/valueLower.description:
The number in the [units](glossary:types/UncertSpan/units) of the span. A file writes either this attribute or [var lower](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varLower) for the lower end, and where it writes neither the interval is open at the bottom.

The report shows it as the left side of the interval.
types/UncertSpan/valueLower.default: the lower end is the element var lower names, or the interval is open at the bottom

rules.message: The attribute 'distrib:valueLower' on an <uncertSpan> must have a value of data type 'double'.

types/UncertSpan/valueUpper.label: valueUpper
types/UncertSpan/valueUpper.summary: the upper end of the interval as a number
types/UncertSpan/valueUpper.description:
The number in the [units](glossary:types/UncertSpan/units) of the span. A file writes either this attribute or [var upper](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varUpper) for the upper end, and where it writes neither the interval is open at the top.

The report shows it as the right side of the interval.
types/UncertSpan/valueUpper.default: the upper end is the element var upper names, or the interval is open at the top

rules.message: The attribute 'distrib:valueUpper' on an <uncertSpan> must have a value of data type 'double'.

types/UncertSpan/var.label: var
types/UncertSpan/var.summary: the element of a single number, which a span does not use
types/UncertSpan/var.description: A span names the elements of its two ends in [var lower](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varLower) and [var upper](glossary:types/UncertSpan/varUpper). The attribute belongs to the [uncert parameter](glossary:types/UncertParameter/var) a span derives from and is left unset by every interval.
types/UncertSpan/var.default: a span names the elements of its ends in var lower and var upper

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'distrib:var' of an <uncertParameter> object must be the identifier of an existing object derived from the 'SBase' class and defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/UncertSpan/varLower.label: varLower
types/UncertSpan/varLower.summary: the element of the model which holds the lower end
types/UncertSpan/varLower.description:
Where the lower end of the interval is a quantity of the model and not a fixed number, the span names that element, the way the [var](glossary:types/UncertParameter/var) of a parameter names one. Its units are the units of the element it names.

The report links the element, and the inspector of that element shows the span under "referenced by".
types/UncertSpan/varLower.default: the lower end is the number in value lower, or the interval is open at the bottom

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'distrib:varLower' of an <uncertSpan> object must be the identifier of an existing object derived from the 'SBase' class and defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/UncertSpan/varUpper.label: varUpper
types/UncertSpan/varUpper.summary: the element of the model which holds the upper end
types/UncertSpan/varUpper.description:
Where the upper end of the interval is a quantity of the model and not a fixed number, the span names that element, the way the [var](glossary:types/UncertParameter/var) of a parameter names one. Its units are the units of the element it names.

The report links the element, and the inspector of that element shows the span under "referenced by".
types/UncertSpan/varUpper.default: the upper end is the number in value upper, or the interval is open at the top

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'distrib:varUpper' of an <uncertSpan> object must be the identifier of an existing object derived from the 'SBase' class and defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/Uncertainty.label: Uncertainty
types/Uncertainty.summary: a set of statistical measures of the value of an element
types/Uncertainty.description:
An uncertainty collects the measures which belong together, for example the mean and the standard deviation of one experiment. Every measure appears at most once in it, so measures from another source belong into another uncertainty of the same element.

The measures do not affect a simulation. They say where a number comes from and how well it is known, which is what a reader of a published model wants to see and what a sampling of the parameters of a model needs.

The report shows every uncertainty as an element of its own, with the table of its measures and a link to the element it describes, and it shows the same table in the inspector of that element.

rules.message: An <uncertainty> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <uncertainty>.
An <uncertainty> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <uncertainty>.

An <uncertainty> object may contain one and only one instance of the <listOfUncertParameters> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Distributions namespaces are permitted on an <uncertainty> object.

types/Uncertainty/uncertParameters.label: uncertParameters
types/Uncertainty/uncertParameters.summary: the statistical measures which make up the uncertainty
types/Uncertainty/uncertParameters.description:
Every parameter names the statistic it describes, for example `mean`, `standardDeviation`, `variance`, `sampleSize`, a span such as `confidenceInterval` or `range`, or the `distribution` the value was drawn from. It gives the statistic either as a number in its value, or as a reference to an element of the model in its variable, and it may carry its own units. A parameter of the type `distribution` carries the math of the distribution or a definition url instead of a value; a parameter of the type `externalParameter` has to carry a definition url and may use everything else next to it, a value, a span, math or parameters of its own.

The report shows every parameter of an uncertainty as a row of the table in the inspector of that uncertainty, with its value or the interval of a span, its units, its definition and its math, and links every parameter to the element it is, where its notes say where the measurement comes from.

rules.message: Apart from the general notes and annotations subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfUncertParameters> container object may only contain <uncertParameter> objects.

An <uncertainty> object may contain one and only one instance of the <listOfUncertParameters> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Distributions namespaces are permitted on an <uncertainty> object.

types/UnitDefinition.label: UnitDefinition
types/UnitDefinition.summary: a named unit built from the base units of SBML
types/UnitDefinition.description:
A unit definition composes a unit from base units, each raised to an exponent, scaled by a power of ten and multiplied by a factor; "millimole per litre per second" is such a product. Its identifier can then be used wherever a model declares units. Unit definitions are optional and a model has to be numerically consistent without them, but they let a reader and a tool check what the numbers mean.

The report renders every unit definition as a formula, in the table and in the inspector, and lists the units it is built from in the inspector.

rules.message: The value of the 'id' field of every <unitDefinition> must be unique across the set of all <unitDefinition>s in the entire model.
The value of the 'id' attribute in a <unitDefinition> must be of type 'UnitSId' and not be identical to any unit predefined in SBML.

A UnitDefinition object must have the required attribute 'id' and may have the optional attributes 'metaid', 'sboTerm' and 'name'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a UnitDefinition object.

types/UnitDefinition/listOfUnits.label: listOfUnits
types/UnitDefinition/listOfUnits.summary: the units the definition multiplies, each with its exponent, scale and multiplier
types/UnitDefinition/listOfUnits.description:
Every unit of the list is one factor of the definition: a base unit of SBML named by its kind, raised to the exponent, scaled by ten to the power of the scale and multiplied by the multiplier. "millimole per litre" is the mole with scale -3 times the litre with exponent -1, and "minute" is the second with multiplier 60. A definition with an empty list of units is an undefined unit, which is not the same as a dimensionless one.

The inspector of a unit definition shows the units as a table of kind, exponent, scale and multiplier next to the formula the report renders from them, so a reader sees what the file says as well as what it means.
types/UnitDefinition/listOfUnits.default: the unit definition is an undefined unit

rules.message: The value of the 'kind' attribute of a <unit> can only be one of the base units enumerated by 'UnitKind'; that is, the SBML unit system is not hierarchical and user-defined units cannot be defined using other user-defined units.
The ListOfUnits container object in a UnitDefinition object is optional, but if present, it must not be empty.
There may be at most one ListOfUnits container objects in a UnitDefinition object.
Apart from the general Notes and Annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML components, a ListOfUnits container object may only contain Unit objects.

A Unit object must have the required attributes 'kind', 'exponent', 'scale' and 'multiplier', and may have the optional attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespace are permitted on a Unit object.

types/UnitDefinition/unitsLatex.label: formula
types/UnitDefinition/unitsLatex.summary: the composed unit rendered as a formula
types/UnitDefinition/unitsLatex.description:
The report multiplies the base units of the definition with their exponent, scale and multiplier and renders the result as a formula, for example millimole per litre per second as a fraction.

The rendered unit is the column "units" of the table of unit definitions and the row "formula" of the inspector, above the units it is built from.

types/UserDefinedConstraint.label: UserDefinedConstraint
types/UserDefinedConstraint.summary: a constraint over a combination of fluxes and parameters, added in Version 3
types/UserDefinedConstraint.description:
The bounds of a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction) constrain one flux at a time, and the stoichiometry of the network constrains the fluxes which share a species. A user defined constraint is everything else a modeller knows: that two reactions run at a fixed ratio, that a set of reactions shares a budget, or that a flux is coupled to a parameter which a simulation changes.

It is a sum of its [components](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent), each of which weighs one model variable, and the sum has to stay between the values of the two [parameters](glossary:types/Parameter) it names as its bounds.

The report shows the user defined constraints of a model in a section of their own, with the table of their components.

rules.message: An <userDefinedConstraint> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <userDefinedConstraint>.

An <userDefinedConstraint> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <userDefinedConstraint>.

An <userDefinedConstraint> object must have the required attributes 'fbc:lowerBound' and 'fbc:upperBound', and may have the optional attributes 'fbc:id' and 'fbc:name'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespaces are permitted on an <userDefinedConstraint> object.

An <userDefinedConstraint> object must contain one and only one instance of the <listOfUserDefinedConstraintComponents> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespaces are permitted on an <userDefinedConstraint> object.

types/UserDefinedConstraint/listOfUserDe.label: listOfUserDefinedConstraintComponents
types/UserDefinedConstraint/listOfUserDe.summary: the weighted variables the constraint is the sum of
types/UserDefinedConstraint/listOfUserDe.description: A constraint which is defined has at least one [component](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent). The report shows them as a table of the variable, the coefficient and the type of every term, with a link to each of them.

rules.message: An <userDefinedConstraint> object must contain one and only one instance of the <listOfUserDefinedConstraintComponents> element. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespaces are permitted on an <userDefinedConstraint> object.

Apart from the general notes and annotations subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfUserDefinedConstraintComponents> container object may only contain <userDefinedConstraintComponent> objects.

types/UserDefinedConstraint/lowerBound.label: lowerBound
types/UserDefinedConstraint/lowerBound.summary: the parameter which holds the smallest value the constraint may take
types/UserDefinedConstraint/lowerBound.description: The attribute is required and names a [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) of the model, the way the lower flux bound of a reaction does, so that a scenario is changed in one place. A constraint whose two bounds name the same parameter is an equality.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:lowerBound' of an <userDefinedConstraint> object must be the identifier of an existing <parameter> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/UserDefinedConstraint/upperBound.label: upperBound
types/UserDefinedConstraint/upperBound.summary: the parameter which holds the largest value the constraint may take
types/UserDefinedConstraint/upperBound.description: The attribute is required and names a [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) of the model. Together with the lower bound it reads `lowerBound <= sum of the components <= upperBound`.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:upperBound' of an <userDefinedConstraint> object must be the identifier of an existing <parameter> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent.label: UserDefinedConstraintComponent
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent.summary: one weighted variable of a user defined constraint
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent.description:
A component is one term of the sum a [user defined constraint](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraint) bounds: the model variable it is about, the [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) which holds the number the variable is multiplied with, and whether the variable enters the sum linearly or quadratically.

The variable is either a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction), whose flux is meant, or a parameter which is not constant, which is how a constraint reaches a quantity the network does not carry.

rules.message: An <userDefinedConstraintComponent> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core attributes 'metaid' and 'sboTerm'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <userDefinedConstraintComponent>.

An <userDefinedConstraintComponent> object may have the optional SBML Level 3 Core subobjects for notes and annotations. No other elements from the SBML Level 3 Core namespaces are permitted on an <userDefinedConstraintComponent>.

An <userDefinedConstraintComponent> object must have the required attributes 'fbc:coefficient', 'fbc:variable' and 'fbc:variableType', and may have the optional attributes 'fbc:id', 'fbc:name' and 'fbc:variable2'. No other attributes from the SBML Level 3 Flux Balance Constraints namespaces are permitted on an <userDefinedConstraintComponent> object.

types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/coe.label: coefficient
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/coe.summary: the parameter which holds the number the variable is multiplied with
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/coe.description: Unlike the coefficient of a [flux objective](glossary:types/FluxObjective), which is a number written into the file, the coefficient of a component is the identifier of a [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter), so that the weights of a constraint can be changed in one place. In a strict model that parameter has to be constant and its value finite.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:coefficient' of an <userDefinedConstraintComponent> object must be the identifier of an existing <parameter> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.label: variable
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.summary: the reaction or the parameter this term of the constraint weighs
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.description: The attribute is required and names either a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction), in which case the term is about its flux, or a [parameter](glossary:types/Parameter) which is not constant. The report links the element it names.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:variable' of an <userDefinedConstraintComponent> object must be the identifier of an existing <reaction> or <parameter> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.label: variable2
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.summary: the second variable of a mixed quadratic term
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.description: A quadratic component which names a second variable weighs the product of the two, `coefficient * v1 * v2`, instead of the square of the first. It is optional and empty in a linear component.
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.default: a quadratic component is the square of its first variable

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:variable2' of an <userDefinedConstraintComponent> object must be the identifier of an existing <reaction> or <parameter> object defined in the enclosing <model> object.

types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.label: variableType
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.summary: whether the variable enters the constraint linearly or quadratically
types/UserDefinedConstraintComponent/var.description: The type is `linear` or `quadratic`, as in a [flux objective](glossary:types/FluxObjective): a quadratic component squares its variable, or multiplies it by the second variable where it names one. It is required.

rules.message: The value of the attribute 'fbc:variableType' of an <userDefinedConstraintComponent> object must conform to the syntax of SBML data type 'FbcVariableType' and may only take on the allowed values of 'FbcVariableType' defined in SBML; that is, the value must be one of the following: 'linear' or 'quadratic'.

types/comp.label: Hierarchical Model Composition (comp)
types/comp.summary: the package which builds a model out of other models
types/comp.description:
A package of SBML Level 3 adds elements and attributes for a domain which not every model needs, and declares itself in the file so that a reader knows whether it has to understand them; this is what makes Level 3 modular instead of one growing language ([Keating et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.15252/msb.20199110)).

The comp package adds composition. A [submodel](glossary:types/Submodel) instantiates another model, a [port](glossary:types/Port) marks the elements through which other models are meant to interact with it, a deletion removes what does not belong in the new context, and a replacement glues an element of the containing model onto an element of a submodel. The models which are instantiated are either model definitions of the same file or [external model definitions](glossary:types/ExternalModelDefinition) pointing at another file.

The report shows the model definitions of a document next to its main model, the submodels and the ports of a model as sections of their own, and the replacements of an element in its inspector.

rules.message: To conform to Version 1 of the Hierarchical Model Composition package specification for SBML Level 3, an SBML document must declare the use of the following XML Namespace: 'http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/comp/version1'

Wherever they appear in an SBML document, elements and attributes from the Hierarchical Model Composition package must be declared either implicitly or explicitly to be in the XML namespace 'http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/comp/version1'
In all SBML documents using the HierarchicalModel Composition package, the SBML object must include a value for the attribute 'comp:required' attribute.
The value of attribute 'comp:required' on the SBML object must be of the data type Boolean.
There may be at most one instance of the <listOfModelDefinitions> within an SBML object that uses the SBML Level 3 Hierarchical Model Composition package.

The various 'ListOf' subobjects within an SBML object are optional, but if present, these container objects must not be empty. Specifically, if any of the following classes of objects is present within the SBML object, it must not be empty: <listOfModelDefinitions> and <listOfExternalModelDefinitions>.
Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfModelDefinitions> container may only contain <modelDefinition> objects.
Apart from the general notes and annotation subobjects permitted on all SBML objects, a <listOfExternalModelDefinitions> container may only contain <externalModelDefinition> objects.
There may be at most one instance of the <listOfExternalModelDefinitions> within an SBML object that uses the SBML Level 3 Hierarchical Model Composition package.
The value of attribute 'comp:required' on the SBML object must be set to 'true'.

types/distrib.label: Distributions (distrib)
types/distrib.summary: the package which records the uncertainty of a value
types/distrib.description:
The distrib package attaches statistical measures to the elements of a model which have a mathematical meaning: a mean, a standard deviation, a variance, a confidence interval or the distribution a value was drawn from. The measures describe the value at the moment it is computed, not how it changes during a simulation.

They do not affect the mathematics of the model. They are a controlled format for the provenance of a number, which a modeller would otherwise write into the notes of an element, and a tool may use them as it uses any other annotation.

The report shows the [uncertainties](glossary:types/Uncertainty) of an element in its inspector and every uncertainty as an element of its own.

rules.message: To conform to the Distributions Package specification for SBML Level 3 Version 1, an SBML document must declare 'http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/distrib/version1' as the XMLNamespace to use for elements of this package.

Wherever they appear in an SBML document, elements and attributes from the Distributions Package must use the 'http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/distrib/version1' namespace, declaring so either explicitly or implicitly.
In all SBML documents using the Distributions Package, the <sbml> object must have the 'distrib:required' attribute.
The value of attribute 'distrib:required' on the <sbml> object must be of data type 'boolean'.
The value of attribute 'distrib:required' on the <sbml> object must be set to 'true'.

types/fbc.label: Flux Balance Constraints (fbc)
types/fbc.summary: the package which describes a constraint based model
types/fbc.description:
A constraint based model does not integrate rate laws over time. It assumes a steady state and chooses the fluxes of the reactions so that an objective function becomes extremal while every flux stays within its bounds, which is what flux balance analysis does with a genome scale reconstruction.

The fbc package holds what such a model needs beyond the core: the lower and the upper flux bound of a [reaction](glossary:types/Reaction), the [objectives](glossary:types/Objective) with their flux objectives, the [gene products](glossary:types/GeneProduct) and the association which relates them to a reaction, and the chemical formula and the charge of a [species](glossary:types/Species). Its three versions write part of it differently: Version 1 states a bound as a [flux bound](glossary:types/FluxBound) of its own, Version 2 makes the two bounds attributes of the reaction which name parameters and adds the gene products, and Version 3 adds the [user defined constraints](glossary:types/UserDefinedConstraint) over several fluxes and the key value pairs which annotate an element.

The report shows the gene products, the objectives, the flux bounds of Version 1 and the user defined constraints of Version 3 as sections of a model of their own, and the fbc attributes of a species and of a reaction in their inspector.

rules.message: To conform to Version 1 of the Flux Balance Constraints package specification for SBML Level 3, an SBML document must declare the use of the following XML Namespace: 'http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/fbc/version1'

Wherever they appear in an SBML document, elements and attributes from the Flux Balance Constraints package must be declared either implicitly or explicitly to be in the XML namespace 'http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/fbc/version1'
In all SBML documents using the Flux Balance Constraints package, the SBML object must include a value for the attribute 'fbc:required'.
The value of attribute 'fbc:required' on the SBML object must be of the data type Boolean.
The value of attribute 'fbc:required' on the SBML object must be set to 'false'.

types/qual.label: Qualitative Models (qual)
types/qual.summary: the package which describes a model whose entities carry a level
types/qual.description:
A qualitative model does not integrate rate laws over time. Its entities carry a level, a whole number which stands for a range of activity, and a rule says which level an entity takes next given the levels of the entities which act on it. It is how a regulatory network is written down when the kinetics are unknown, which is the usual case for a network of genes, and it covers the logical models of the Boolean school as well as Petri nets.

The qual package holds what such a model needs beyond the core: the [qualitative species](glossary:types/QualitativeSpecies) with their levels, and the [transitions](glossary:types/Transition) with the [inputs](glossary:types/Input) they read, the [outputs](glossary:types/Output) they change and the [function terms](glossary:types/FunctionTerm) which decide between them.

The report shows the qualitative species and the transitions of a model as sections of their own, the inputs of a transition with the sign of their influence, and the function terms as the transition table they are.

rules.message: To conform to Version 1 of the Qualitative Models package specification for SBML Level 3, an SBML document must declare the use of the following XML Namespace: 'http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/qual/version1'

Wherever they appear in an SBML document, elements and attributes from the Qualitative Models package must be declared either implicitly or explicitly to be in the XML namespace 'http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/qual/version1'
In all SBML documents using the Qualitative Models package, the SBML object must include a value for the attribute 'qual:required' attribute.
The value of attribute 'qual:required' on the SBML object must be of the data type Boolean.
The value of attribute 'qual:required' on the SBML object must be set to 'true' if if the model contains any <transition> objects.
